AcceptEngagementInvitation.name: AcceptEngagementInvitation
AcceptEngagementInvitation.documentation: Use the AcceptEngagementInvitation action to accept an engagement invitation shared by AWS. Accepting the invitation indicates your willingness to participate in the engagement, granting you access to all engagement-related data.

AssignOpportunity.name: AssignOpportunity
AssignOpportunity.documentation:
Enables you to reassign an existing Opportunity to another user within your Partner Central account. The specified user receives the opportunity, and it appears on their Partner Central dashboard, allowing them to take necessary actions or proceed with the opportunity.

This is useful for distributing opportunities to the appropriate team members or departments within your organization, ensuring that each opportunity is handled by the right person. By default, the opportunity owner is the one who creates it. Currently, there's no API to enumerate the list of available users.

AssociateOpportunity.name: AssociateOpportunity
AssociateOpportunity.documentation:
Enables you to create a formal association between an Opportunity and various related entities, enriching the context and details of the opportunity for better collaboration and decision making. You can associate an opportunity with the following entity types:

  • Partner Solution: A software product or consulting practice created and delivered by Partners. Partner Solutions help customers address business challenges using Amazon Web Services services.

  • Amazon Web Services Products: Amazon Web Services offers many products and services that provide scalable, reliable, and cost-effective infrastructure solutions. For the latest list of Amazon Web Services products, see Amazon Web Services products.

  • Amazon Web Services Marketplace private offer: Allows Amazon Web Services Marketplace sellers to extend custom pricing and terms to individual Amazon Web Services customers. Sellers can negotiate custom prices, payment schedules, and end user license terms through private offers, enabling Amazon Web Services customers to acquire software solutions tailored to their specific needs. For more information, see Private offers in Amazon Web Services Marketplace.

To obtain identifiers for these entities, use the following methods:

  • Solution: Use the ListSolutions operation.

  • AWS Products: For the latest list of Amazon Web Services products, see Amazon Web Services products.

  • Amazon Web Services Marketplace private offer: Use the Using the Amazon Web Services Marketplace Catalog API to list entities. Specifically, use the ListEntities operation to retrieve a list of private offers. The request returns the details of available private offers. For more information, see ListEntities.

CreateCustomerAccount.name: CreateCustomerAccount
CreateCustomerAccount.documentation:
Use CreateCustomerAccount to map a customer account from your records to an AWS customer. Provide details about the customer, such as the company name and website. AWS then matches the account to a customer and adds enrichment information about it.

Matching runs asynchronously. The response returns the new customer account with a status of PENDING. Use GetCustomerAccount to check the result and read the enrichment information.

CreateEngagement.name: CreateEngagement
CreateEngagement.documentation: The CreateEngagement action allows you to create an Engagement, which serves as a collaborative space between different parties such as AWS Partners and AWS Sellers. This action automatically adds the caller's AWS account as an active member of the newly created Engagement.

CreateEngagementContext.name: CreateEngagementContext
CreateEngagementContext.documentation: Creates a new context within an existing engagement. This action allows you to add contextual information such as customer projects or documents to an engagement, providing additional details that help facilitate collaboration between engagement members.

CreateEngagementInvitation.name: CreateEngagementInvitation
CreateEngagementInvitation.documentation: This action creates an invitation from a sender to a single receiver to join an engagement.

CreateOpportunity.name: CreateOpportunity
CreateOpportunity.documentation:
Creates an Opportunity record in Partner Central. Use this operation to create a potential business opportunity for submission to Amazon Web Services. Creating an opportunity sets Lifecycle.ReviewStatus to Pending Submission.

To submit an opportunity, follow these steps:

  1. To create the opportunity, use CreateOpportunity.

  2. To associate a solution with the opportunity, use AssociateOpportunity.

  3. To start the engagement with AWS, use StartEngagementFromOpportunity.

After submission, you can't edit the opportunity until the review is complete. But opportunities in the Pending Submission state must have complete details. You can update the opportunity while it's in the Pending Submission state.

There's a set of mandatory fields to create opportunities, but consider providing optional fields to enrich the opportunity record.

CreateResourceSnapshot.name: CreateResourceSnapshot
CreateResourceSnapshot.documentation: This action allows you to create an immutable snapshot of a specific resource, such as an opportunity, within the context of an engagement. The snapshot captures a subset of the resource's data based on the schema defined by the provided template.

CreateResourceSnapshotJob.name: CreateResourceSnapshotJob
CreateResourceSnapshotJob.documentation: Use this action to create a job to generate a snapshot of the specified resource within an engagement. It initiates an asynchronous process to create a resource snapshot. The job creates a new snapshot only if the resource state has changed, adhering to the same access control and immutability rules as direct snapshot creation.

DeleteCustomerAccount.name: DeleteCustomerAccount
DeleteCustomerAccount.documentation: Use DeleteCustomerAccount to delete a customer account. This operation is idempotent. Deleting a customer account that was already deleted succeeds.

DeleteResourceSnapshotJob.name: DeleteResourceSnapshotJob
DeleteResourceSnapshotJob.documentation: Use this action to deletes a previously created resource snapshot job. The job must be in a stopped state before it can be deleted.

DisassociateOpportunity.name: DisassociateOpportunity
DisassociateOpportunity.documentation:
Allows you to remove an existing association between an Opportunity and related entities, such as a Partner Solution, Amazon Web Services product, or an Amazon Web Services Marketplace offer. This operation is the counterpart to AssociateOpportunity, and it provides flexibility to manage associations as business needs change.

Use this operation to update the associations of an Opportunity due to changes in the related entities, or if an association was made in error. Ensuring accurate associations helps maintain clarity and accuracy to track and manage business opportunities. When you replace an entity, first attach the new entity and then disassociate the one to be removed, especially if it's the last remaining entity that's required.

GetAwsOpportunitySummary.name: GetAwsOpportunitySummary
GetAwsOpportunitySummary.documentation: Retrieves a summary of an AWS Opportunity. This summary includes high-level details about the opportunity sourced from AWS, such as lifecycle information, customer details, and involvement type. It is useful for tracking updates on the AWS opportunity corresponding to an opportunity in the partner's account.

GetCustomerAccount.name: GetCustomerAccount
GetCustomerAccount.documentation: Use GetCustomerAccount to retrieve the details of a customer account, including the customer information that you provided, the enrichment status, and the enrichment information that AWS provides when the status is ENRICHED.

GetCustomerAccountBulkJob.name: GetCustomerAccountBulkJob
GetCustomerAccountBulkJob.documentation: Use GetCustomerAccountBulkJob to retrieve the status and record counts of a bulk job.

GetCustomerAccountBulkJobReportUrl.name: GetCustomerAccountBulkJobReportUrl
GetCustomerAccountBulkJobReportUrl.documentation:
Use GetCustomerAccountBulkJobReportUrl to get a temporary URL for downloading the report of a bulk job, such as the list of records that failed. A report is available only after the job is COMPLETED or FAILED. For a job that is still running, the request fails with a ConflictException.

The report is generated on request. If ReportStatus is not AVAILABLE, call the operation again later.

GetCustomerAccountStatistics.name: GetCustomerAccountStatistics
GetCustomerAccountStatistics.documentation: Use GetCustomerAccountStatistics to count your customer accounts and group them by fields such as industry, geography, or enrichment status. You can use the same filters as SearchCustomerAccounts.

GetEngagement.name: GetEngagement
GetEngagement.documentation: Use this action to retrieve the engagement record for a given EngagementIdentifier.

GetEngagementInvitation.name: GetEngagementInvitation
GetEngagementInvitation.documentation: Retrieves the details of an engagement invitation shared by AWS with a partner. The information includes aspects such as customer, project details, and lifecycle information. To connect an engagement invitation with an opportunity, match the invitation’s Payload.Project.Title with opportunity Project.Title.

GetOpportunity.name: GetOpportunity
GetOpportunity.documentation:
Fetches the Opportunity record from Partner Central by a given Identifier.

Use the ListOpportunities action or the event notification (from Amazon EventBridge) to obtain this identifier.

GetOpportunityBulkJobReportUrl.name: GetOpportunityBulkJobReportUrl
GetOpportunityBulkJobReportUrl.documentation:
Gets the status of the failed-records report for a finished opportunity bulk job and, when the report is ready, a temporary URL to download it.

A report is available only after the job is COMPLETED or FAILED. The URL expires after 15 minutes, and the report expires after about 7 days.

GetProspectingFromEngagementTask.name: GetProspectingFromEngagementTask
GetProspectingFromEngagementTask.documentation: Retrieves the details and current status of a prospecting task previously started with StartProspectingFromEngagementTask to enable polling for completion and access to per-engagement processing results.

GetResourceSnapshot.name: GetResourceSnapshot
GetResourceSnapshot.documentation: Use this action to retrieve a specific snapshot record.

GetResourceSnapshotJob.name: GetResourceSnapshotJob
GetResourceSnapshotJob.documentation: Use this action to retrieves information about a specific resource snapshot job.

GetSellingSystemSettings.name: GetSellingSystemSettings
GetSellingSystemSettings.documentation: Retrieves the currently set system settings, which include the IAM Role used for resource snapshot jobs.

ListCustomerAccountBulkJobResults.name: ListCustomerAccountBulkJobResults
ListCustomerAccountBulkJobResults.documentation:
Use ListCustomerAccountBulkJobResults to list the outcome of each record in a bulk job. You can filter the results to records that succeeded or failed. A job that failed before it processed any records returns an empty list.

Results are paginated. Use NextToken to retrieve additional results.

ListCustomerAccountBulkJobs.name: ListCustomerAccountBulkJobs
ListCustomerAccountBulkJobs.documentation:
Use ListCustomerAccountBulkJobs to list the bulk jobs in the specified catalog. You can filter the results by job identifier or status.

Results are paginated. Use NextToken to retrieve additional results.

ListEngagementByAcceptingInvitationTasks.name: ListEngagementByAcceptingInvitationTasks
ListEngagementByAcceptingInvitationTasks.documentation: Lists all in-progress, completed, or failed StartEngagementByAcceptingInvitationTask tasks that were initiated by the caller's account.

ListEngagementFromOpportunityTasks.name: ListEngagementFromOpportunityTasks
ListEngagementFromOpportunityTasks.documentation: Lists all in-progress, completed, or failed EngagementFromOpportunity tasks that were initiated by the caller's account.

ListEngagementGroups.name: ListEngagementGroups
ListEngagementGroups.documentation: Lists the active, fully curated AWS Partner Central engagement groups that are available to you in the specified catalog. An engagement group is a curated set of engagements that share common characteristics, such as customer geography, industry, or solution category. To retrieve the engagements in a group, pass the group Id to SearchEngagements as GroupId, and use NextToken to retrieve additional pages of groups.

ListEngagementInvitations.name: ListEngagementInvitations
ListEngagementInvitations.documentation: Retrieves a list of engagement invitations sent to the partner. This allows partners to view all pending or past engagement invitations, helping them track opportunities shared by AWS.

ListEngagementMembers.name: ListEngagementMembers
ListEngagementMembers.documentation: Retrieves the details of member partners in an Engagement. This operation can only be invoked by members of the Engagement. The ListEngagementMembers operation allows you to fetch information about the members of a specific Engagement. This action is restricted to members of the Engagement being queried.

ListEngagementResourceAssociations.name: ListEngagementResourceAssociations
ListEngagementResourceAssociations.documentation: Lists the associations between resources and engagements where the caller is a member and has at least one snapshot in the engagement.

ListEngagements.name: ListEngagements
ListEngagements.documentation: This action allows users to retrieve a list of Engagement records from Partner Central. This action can be used to manage and track various engagements across different stages of the partner selling process.

ListOpportunities.name: ListOpportunities
ListOpportunities.documentation:
This request accepts a list of filters that retrieve opportunity subsets as well as sort options. This feature is available to partners from Partner Central using the ListOpportunities API action.

To synchronize your system with Amazon Web Services, list only the opportunities that were newly created or updated. We recommend you rely on events emitted by the service into your Amazon Web Services account’s Amazon EventBridge default event bus. You can also use the ListOpportunities action.

We recommend the following approach:

  1. Find the latest LastModifiedDate that you stored, and only use the values that came from Amazon Web Services. Don’t use values generated by your system.

  2. When you send a ListOpportunities request, submit the date in ISO 8601 format in the AfterLastModifiedDate filter.

  3. Amazon Web Services only returns opportunities created or updated on or after that date and time. Use NextToken to iterate over all pages.

ListOpportunityBulkJobResults.name: ListOpportunityBulkJobResults
ListOpportunityBulkJobResults.documentation:
Lists the outcome of each record in an opportunity bulk job. You can filter the results by record status.

Results are paginated. Use NextToken to retrieve additional results.

ListOpportunityBulkJobs.name: ListOpportunityBulkJobs
ListOpportunityBulkJobs.documentation:
Lists the opportunity bulk jobs in the specified catalog, newest first. You can filter the results by job identifier or status.

Results are paginated. Use NextToken to retrieve additional results.

ListOpportunityFromEngagementTasks.name: ListOpportunityFromEngagementTasks
ListOpportunityFromEngagementTasks.documentation: Lists all in-progress, completed, or failed opportunity creation tasks from engagements that were initiated by the caller's account.

ListProspectingFromEngagementTasks.name: ListProspectingFromEngagementTasks
ListProspectingFromEngagementTasks.documentation: Lists all prospecting tasks initiated by the caller's account. Supports optional filters by task identifier, task name, or start time range. Results can be sorted using configurable options. The response is paginated. Use the NextToken value from each response to retrieve subsequent pages.

ListResourceSnapshotJobs.name: ListResourceSnapshotJobs
ListResourceSnapshotJobs.documentation: Lists resource snapshot jobs owned by the customer. This operation supports various filtering scenarios, including listing all jobs owned by the caller, jobs for a specific engagement, jobs with a specific status, or any combination of these filters.

ListResourceSnapshots.name: ListResourceSnapshots
ListResourceSnapshots.documentation:
Retrieves a list of resource view snapshots based on specified criteria. This operation supports various use cases, including:

  • Fetching all snapshots associated with an engagement.

  • Retrieving snapshots of a specific resource type within an engagement.

  • Obtaining snapshots for a particular resource using a specified template.

  • Accessing the latest snapshot of a resource within an engagement.

  • Filtering snapshots by resource owner.

ListSolutions.name: ListSolutions
ListSolutions.documentation: Retrieves a list of Partner Solutions that the partner registered on Partner Central. This API is used to generate a list of solutions that an end user selects from for association with an opportunity.

ListTagsForResource.name: ListTagsForResource
ListTagsForResource.documentation: Returns a list of tags for a resource.

PutSellingSystemSettings.name: PutSellingSystemSettings
PutSellingSystemSettings.documentation: Updates the currently set system settings, which include the IAM Role used for resource snapshot jobs.

RejectEngagementInvitation.name: RejectEngagementInvitation
RejectEngagementInvitation.documentation: This action rejects an EngagementInvitation that AWS shared. Rejecting an invitation indicates that the partner doesn't want to pursue the opportunity, and all related data will become inaccessible thereafter.

SearchCustomerAccounts.name: SearchCustomerAccounts
SearchCustomerAccounts.documentation:
Use SearchCustomerAccounts to find customer accounts in the specified catalog. You can filter the results by fields such as enrichment status, industry, geography, and creation date, and sort them by company name, date, or score.

Results are paginated. Use NextToken to retrieve additional results.

SearchEngagements.name: SearchEngagements
SearchEngagements.documentation: Searches the engagements in AWS Partner Central that match your criteria, such as customer industry or geography. You can combine a free-text Keyword, a structured Filter tree, an engagement group (GroupId), and Sort options, and each search criterion that you specify narrows the results. Results are paginated, so use NextToken to retrieve additional results.

SearchOpportunities.name: SearchOpportunities
SearchOpportunities.documentation:
The SearchOpportunities operation in the AWS Partner Central Selling API searches and filters the opportunities available to you in AWS Partner Central.

You can optionally provide a free-text Keyword, a structured Filter tree, and Sort options. The operation returns a curated summary view of each matching opportunity. If you supply both Keyword and Filter, the operation combines them with a logical AND, so each one narrows the result set.

Results are paginated. Use the NextToken parameter to retrieve additional pages of results.

StartCustomerAccountBulkJob.name: StartCustomerAccountBulkJob
StartCustomerAccountBulkJob.documentation:
Use StartCustomerAccountBulkJob to create many customer accounts from a single file. The job starts processing as soon as it is created.

Use GetCustomerAccountBulkJob to track progress, ListCustomerAccountBulkJobResults to review the outcome of each record, and GetCustomerAccountBulkJobReportUrl to download a report when the job finishes.

StartEngagementByAcceptingInvitationTask.name: StartEngagementByAcceptingInvitationTask
StartEngagementByAcceptingInvitationTask.documentation: This action starts the engagement by accepting an EngagementInvitation. The task is asynchronous and involves the following steps: accepting the invitation, creating an opportunity in the partner’s account from the AWS opportunity, and copying details for tracking. When completed, an Opportunity Created event is generated, indicating that the opportunity has been successfully created in the partner's account.

StartEngagementFromOpportunityTask.name: StartEngagementFromOpportunityTask
StartEngagementFromOpportunityTask.documentation: Similar to StartEngagementByAcceptingInvitationTask, this action is asynchronous and performs multiple steps before completion. This action orchestrates a comprehensive workflow that combines multiple API operations into a single task to create and initiate an engagement from an existing opportunity. It automatically executes a sequence of operations including GetOpportunity, CreateEngagement (if it doesn't exist), CreateResourceSnapshot, CreateResourceSnapshotJob, CreateEngagementInvitation (if not already invited/accepted), and SubmitOpportunity.

StartOpportunityBulkJob.name: StartOpportunityBulkJob
StartOpportunityBulkJob.documentation:
The StartOpportunityBulkJob operation creates or updates many opportunities in AWS Partner Central (Partner Central) from a single CSV file. The column headers in the file determine whether the job creates or updates opportunities.

Returns a JobId for the job. Use ListOpportunityBulkJobs to track the job, ListOpportunityBulkJobResults to review each record, and GetOpportunityBulkJobReportUrl to download a report of the failed records.

StartOpportunityFromEngagementTask.name: StartOpportunityFromEngagementTask
StartOpportunityFromEngagementTask.documentation: This action creates an opportunity from an existing engagement context. The task is asynchronous and orchestrates the process of converting engagement contextual information into a structured opportunity record within the partner's account.

StartProspectingFromEngagementTask.name: StartProspectingFromEngagementTask
StartProspectingFromEngagementTask.documentation: Starts a task to convert one or more engagement contexts into new prospecting leads. The task runs asynchronously. To poll for status, use GetProspectingFromEngagementTask, or use ListProspectingFromEngagementTasks to monitor multiple tasks.

StartResourceSnapshotJob.name: StartResourceSnapshotJob
StartResourceSnapshotJob.documentation: Starts a resource snapshot job that has been previously created.

StopResourceSnapshotJob.name: StopResourceSnapshotJob
StopResourceSnapshotJob.documentation: Stops a resource snapshot job. The job must be started prior to being stopped.

SubmitOpportunity.name: SubmitOpportunity
SubmitOpportunity.documentation: Use this action to submit an Opportunity that was previously created by partner for AWS review. After you perform this action, the Opportunity becomes non-editable until it is reviewed by AWS and has LifeCycle.ReviewStatus as either Approved or Action Required.

TagResource.name: TagResource
TagResource.documentation: Assigns one or more tags (key-value pairs) to the specified resource.

UntagResource.name: UntagResource
UntagResource.documentation: Removes a tag or tags from a resource.

UpdateCustomerAccount.name: UpdateCustomerAccount
UpdateCustomerAccount.documentation:
Use UpdateCustomerAccount to replace the customer information on an existing customer account. AWS matches the account again with the updated information.

To prevent concurrent changes from overwriting each other, specify the LastModifiedDate value that you last read for the account. If the account changed since then, the request fails with a ConflictException.

UpdateEngagementContext.name: UpdateEngagementContext
UpdateEngagementContext.documentation: Updates the context information for an existing engagement with new or modified data.

UpdateOpportunity.name: UpdateOpportunity
UpdateOpportunity.documentation:
Updates the Opportunity record identified by a given Identifier. This operation allows you to modify the details of an existing opportunity to reflect the latest information and progress. Use this action to keep the opportunity record up-to-date and accurate.

When you perform updates, include the entire payload with each request. If any field is omitted, the API assumes that the field is set to null. The best practice is to always perform a GetOpportunity to retrieve the latest values, then send the complete payload with the updated values to be changed.

Catalog.documentation: The CatalogType parameter specifies the catalog associated with the engagement invitation. Accepted values are AWS and Sandbox, which determine the environment in which the engagement invitation is managed.

Identifier.documentation: The Identifier parameter in the AcceptEngagementInvitationRequest specifies the unique identifier of the EngagementInvitation to be accepted. Providing the correct identifier ensures that the intended invitation is accepted.

AcceptEngagementInvitationRequest.documentation: Contains the request parameters for the AcceptEngagementInvitation operation.

Message.documentation: A message that describes why access was denied.

Reason.documentation: The reason why access was denied for the requested operation.

AccessDeniedException.documentation:
This error occurs when you don't have permission to perform the requested action.

You don’t have access to this action or resource. Review IAM policies or contact your AWS administrator for assistance.

AccessDeniedExceptionErrorCode.documentation: The code that identifies why AWS Partner Central denied access to the requested operation.

OtherIndustry.documentation: Specifies the end Customer's industry associated with the Opportunity, when the selected value in the Industry field is Other.

CompanyName.documentation: Specifies the end Customer's company name associated with the Opportunity.

WebsiteUrl.documentation: Specifies the end customer's company website URL associated with the Opportunity. This value is crucial to map the customer within the Amazon Web Services CRM system. This field is required in all cases except when the opportunity is related to national security.

AwsAccountId.documentation: Specifies the Customer Amazon Web Services account ID associated with the Opportunity.

Address.documentation: Specifies the end Customer's address details associated with the Opportunity.

Account.documentation: Specifies the Customer's account details associated with the Opportunity.

WebsiteUrl.documentation: The website URL of the customer company.

CountryCode.documentation: The country of the customer company, as an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code.

AccountCustomer.documentation: A snapshot of the customer company's identity for an account-planning engagement. The caller can supply these details so that an account can be identified even when it isn't yet mapped to an AWS account.

AccountIdentifier.documentation: The identifier of the customer account that the plan concerns, as an Amazon Resource Name (ARN) or a customer account identifier.

Customer.documentation: A caller-supplied snapshot of the customer company's identity, so that the receiver can tell which account the plan concerns even when the account isn't yet mapped to an AWS account.

SenderContacts.documentation: The sender's contact information for this account plan.

PreferredContact.documentation: When the sender prefers to be contacted about this account plan. This information is advisory.

AccountPlanningInvitationPayload.documentation: The content of an account-planning invitation. It carries what the invited party needs to identify which account the plan concerns, because the receiver can't read the account resource directly. The account can be named by its identifier, by a customer identity snapshot, or both.

Alias.documentation: Represents the alias of the partner account receiving the Engagement Invitation, making it easier to identify and track the recipient in reports or logs.

AwsAccountId.documentation: Indicates the AWS account ID of the partner who received the Engagement Invitation. This is a unique identifier for managing engagements with specific AWS accounts.

AccountReceiver.documentation: Contains the account details of the partner who received the Engagement Invitation, including the AWS account ID and company name.

Industry.documentation:
Specifies which industry the end Customer belongs to associated with the Opportunity. It refers to the category or sector that the customer's business operates in.

To submit a value outside the picklist, use Other.

Conditionally mandatory if Other is selected for Industry Vertical in LOVs.

OtherIndustry.documentation: Specifies the end Customer's industry associated with the Opportunity, when the selected value in the Industry field is Other. This field is relevant when the customer's industry doesn't fall under the predefined picklist values and requires a custom description.

CompanyName.documentation: Specifies the end Customer's company name associated with the Opportunity.

WebsiteUrl.documentation: Specifies the end customer's company website URL associated with the Opportunity. This value is crucial to map the customer within the Amazon Web Services CRM system.

Address.documentation: Specifies the end Customer's address details associated with the Opportunity.

AccountSummary.documentation: An object that contains an Account's subset of fields.

AccountSummaryCompanyNameString.documentation: The name of a person or a company.

AccountWebsiteUrl.documentation: The website URL of the customer's company.

AddressSummaryCityString.documentation: One part of a postal address, such as a street line, a city, a state or region, or a postal code.

AddressSummaryPostalCodeString.documentation: One part of a postal address, such as a street line, a city, a state or region, or a postal code.

AggregatableField.documentation: The fields that you can group customer accounts by in GetCustomerAccountStatistics.

GroupBy.documentation: The field to group the customer accounts by. Specify one field.

AggregationRequest.documentation: Groups customer accounts by the values of a field.

GroupBy.documentation: The field that the customer accounts are grouped by.

Buckets.documentation: The groups of customer accounts, one for each value of the field, with the number of accounts in each group.

OtherCount.documentation: The number of customer accounts that have a value not included in Buckets.

AggregationResult.documentation: The result of an aggregation. It includes the grouped field, the number of customer accounts for each value, and the number of accounts with other values.

Amount.documentation: A monetary amount written as a decimal number with up to two digits after the decimal point.

key.documentation: The name of the AWS program or modernization pathway that the spend amount maps to.

value.documentation: The spend amount that maps to the AWS program or modernization pathway.

AmountMap.documentation: Maps spend amounts to AWS programs and modernization pathways.

ApnPrograms.documentation: A list of the AWS Partner Network (APN) programs that the opportunity relates to.

Catalog.documentation: Specifies the catalog associated with the request. This field takes a string value from a predefined list: AWS or Sandbox. The catalog determines which environment the opportunity is assigned in. Use AWS to assign real opportunities in the Amazon Web Services catalog, and Sandbox for testing in secure, isolated environments.

Identifier.documentation: Requires the Opportunity's unique identifier when you want to assign it to another user. Provide the correct identifier so the intended opportunity is reassigned.

Assignee.documentation: Specifies the user or team member responsible for managing the assigned opportunity. This field identifies the Assignee based on the partner's internal team structure. Ensure that the email address is associated with a registered user in your Partner Central account.

AssignOpportunityRequest.documentation: Contains the request parameters for the AssignOpportunity operation.

Email.documentation: Provides the email address of the assignee. This email is used for communications and notifications related to the opportunity.

FirstName.documentation: Specifies the first name of the assignee managing the opportunity. The system automatically retrieves this value from the user profile by referencing the associated email address.

LastName.documentation: Specifies the last name of the assignee managing the opportunity. The system automatically retrieves this value from the user profile by referencing the associated email address.

Phone.documentation: Specifies the contact phone number of the assignee responsible for the opportunity or engagement. This field enables direct communication for time-sensitive matters and facilitates coordination between AWS and partner teams.

BusinessTitle.documentation: Specifies the business title of the assignee managing the opportunity. This helps clarify the individual's role and responsibilities within the organization. Use the value PartnerAccountManager to update details of the opportunity owner.

AssigneeContact.documentation: Represents the contact details of the individual assigned to manage the opportunity within the partner organization. This helps to ensure that there is a point of contact for the opportunity's progress.

AssigneeContactFirstNameString.documentation: The name of a person or a company.

AssigneeContactLastNameString.documentation: The name of a person or a company.

Catalog.documentation: Specifies the catalog associated with the request. This field takes a string value from a predefined list: AWS or Sandbox. The catalog determines which environment the opportunity association is made in. Use AWS to associate opportunities in the Amazon Web Services catalog, and Sandbox for testing in secure, isolated environments.

OpportunityIdentifier.documentation: Requires the Opportunity's unique identifier when you want to associate it with a related entity. Provide the correct identifier so the intended opportunity is updated with the association.

RelatedEntityType.documentation: Specifies the entity type that you're associating with the Opportunity. This helps to categorize and properly process the association.

RelatedEntityIdentifier.documentation: Requires the related entity's unique identifier when you want to associate it with the Opportunity. For Amazon Web Services Marketplace entities, provide the Amazon Resource Name (ARN). Use the Amazon Web Services Marketplace API to obtain the ARN.

AssociateOpportunityRequest.documentation: Contains the request parameters for the AssociateOpportunity operation.

AwsAccount.documentation: An AWS account ID or an alias for an AWS account. An account ID has 12 digits, and an alias has up to 12 characters.

AwsAccountIdOrAliasList.documentation: A list of AWS account IDs or aliases.

AwsAccountList.documentation: A list of AWS account IDs or aliases.

AwsClosedLostReason.documentation: The reason that AWS gives for closing an opportunity as lost.

Insights.documentation: Insights that AWS computes for the customer.

AwsEnrichment.documentation: The information that we provide about the matched customer, in addition to the details that you supplied. Present only when EnrichmentStatus is ENRICHED.

Industry.documentation: The industry of the customer, as classified by AWS.

SubIndustry.documentation: The sub-industry of the customer, as classified by AWS.

Sector.documentation: The sector of the customer, as classified by AWS.

Segment.documentation: The market segment of the customer, as classified by AWS.

Region.documentation: The region of the customer, as classified by AWS.

SubRegion.documentation: The sub-region of the customer, as classified by AWS.

Geo.documentation: The geographic area of the customer, as classified by AWS.

CustomerAccountPlanningQualification.documentation: Indicates whether the customer qualifies for account planning with AWS.

EligiblePrograms.documentation: The AWS programs that the customer is eligible for.

AwsEnrichmentCustomer.documentation: Recorded facts that we hold about the matched customer, such as the industry, sector, company size, and region.

Industry.documentation: The industry of the customer, as classified by AWS.

AccountPlanningQualification.documentation: Indicates whether the customer qualifies for account planning with AWS.

EligiblePrograms.documentation: The AWS programs that the customer is eligible for.

Geo.documentation: The geographic area of the customer, as classified by AWS.

Segment.documentation: The market segment of the customer, as classified by AWS.

AwsEnrichmentCustomerSummary.documentation: Recorded facts about the matched customer for an account in search results. It carries the fields that you can filter and group by.

MarketplaceEngagementScore.documentation: The level of engagement of the customer with AWS Marketplace. Valid values are High, Medium, and Low.

SolutionCategory.documentation: The category of the solution that AWS recommends for the customer.

SolutionScore.documentation: The likelihood that the customer adopts the recommended solution. Valid values are High, Medium, and Low.

SolutionSubCategory.documentation: The sub-category of the solution that AWS recommends for the customer.

AwsEnrichmentInsights.documentation: Values that we compute about the matched customer, such as the marketplace engagement score and the solution propensity. These differ from the recorded facts in Customer.

MarketplaceEngagementScore.documentation: The level of engagement of the customer with AWS Marketplace. Valid values are High, Medium, and Low.

SolutionCategory.documentation: The category of the solution that AWS recommends for the customer.

SolutionScore.documentation: The likelihood that the customer adopts the recommended solution. Valid values are High, Medium, and Low.

AwsEnrichmentInsightsSummary.documentation: Computed values about the matched customer for an account in search results. It carries the fields that you can sort and filter by.

Customer.documentation: Information about the customer that AWS provides.

Insights.documentation: Insights that AWS computes for the customer.

AwsEnrichmentSummary.documentation: The AWS enrichment information for an account in search results. It carries a reduced set of fields compared to the enrichment information that GetCustomerAccount returns. Present only when EnrichmentStatus is ENRICHED.

AwsFundingUsed.documentation: Specifies whether a marketing development fund (MDF) funds the marketing activity. The value is Yes if an MDF funds the activity, or No if it doesn't.

AwsMarketplaceOfferIdentifier.documentation: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that identifies an AWS Marketplace offer.

AwsMarketplaceOfferIdentifiers.documentation: A list of Amazon Resource Names (ARNs) that identify AWS Marketplace offers.

AwsMarketplaceOfferSetIdentifier.documentation: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that identifies an AWS Marketplace offer set.

AwsMarketplaceOfferSetIdentifiers.documentation: A list of Amazon Resource Names (ARNs) that identify AWS Marketplace offer sets.

AwsMarketplaceProductArn.documentation: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that identifies an AWS Marketplace product.

AwsMarketplaceProductIdentifiers.documentation: A list of Amazon Resource Names (ARNs) that identify AWS Marketplace products.

AwsMarketplaceSolutionArn.documentation: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that identifies an AWS Marketplace solution.

AwsMarketplaceSolutionIdentifier.documentation: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that identifies an AWS Marketplace solution.

AwsMarketplaceSolutionIdentifiers.documentation: A list of Amazon Resource Names (ARNs) that identify AWS Marketplace solutions.

AwsMaturity.documentation: The customer's level of experience with and adoption of AWS services.

AwsMemberBusinessTitle.documentation: The business title of an AWS team member who works on the opportunity.

Contacts.documentation: Provides a list of customer contacts involved in the opportunity. These contacts may include decision makers, influencers, and other stakeholders within the customer's organization.

AwsOpportunityCustomer.documentation: Represents the customer associated with the AWS opportunity. This field captures key details about the customer that are necessary for managing the opportunity.

NextBestActions.documentation: Provides recommendations from AWS on the next best actions to take in order to move the opportunity forward and increase the likelihood of success.

EngagementScore.documentation: Represents a score assigned by AWS to indicate the level of engagement and potential success for the opportunity. This score helps partners prioritize their efforts.

AwsProductsSpendInsightsBySource.documentation: Source-separated spend insights that provide independent analysis for AWS recommendations and partner estimates.

OpportunityQuality.documentation: Opportunity quality assessment. Null if not yet scored.

Recommendations.documentation: List of recommendations from various agent-driven sources.

AwsOpportunityInsights.documentation: Contains insights provided by AWS for the opportunity, offering recommendations and analysis that can help the partner optimize their engagement and strategy.

TargetCloseDate.documentation: Indicates the expected date by which the opportunity is projected to close. This field helps in planning resources and timelines for both the partner and AWS.

ClosedLostReason.documentation: Indicates the reason why an opportunity was marked as Closed Lost. This helps in understanding the context behind the lost opportunity and aids in refining future strategies.

Stage.documentation: Represents the current stage of the opportunity in its lifecycle, such as Qualification, Validation, or Closed Won. This helps in understanding the opportunity's progress.

NextSteps.documentation: Specifies the immediate next steps required to progress the opportunity. These steps are based on AWS guidance and the current stage of the opportunity.

NextStepsHistory.documentation: Provides a historical log of previous next steps that were taken to move the opportunity forward. This helps in tracking the decision-making process and identifying any delays or obstacles encountered.

AwsOpportunityLifeCycle.documentation: Tracks the lifecycle of the AWS opportunity, including stages such as qualification, validation, and closure. This field helps partners understand the current status and progression of the opportunity.

ExpectedCustomerSpend.documentation: Indicates the expected spending by the customer over the course of the project. This value helps partners and AWS estimate the financial impact of the opportunity. Use the AWS Pricing Calculator to create an estimate of the customer’s total spend. If only annual recurring revenue (ARR) is available, distribute it across 12 months to provide an average monthly value.

AwsPartition.documentation: AWS partition where the opportunity will be deployed. Possible values: aws-eusc for AWS European Sovereign Cloud, null for all other partitions.

AwsOpportunityProject.documentation: Captures details about the project associated with the opportunity, including objectives, scope, and customer requirements.

AwsProducts.documentation: Specifies the AWS products associated with the opportunity. This field helps track the specific products that are part of the proposed solution.

Solutions.documentation: Specifies the partner solutions related to the opportunity. These solutions represent the partner's offerings that are being positioned as part of the overall AWS opportunity.

AwsMarketplaceSolutions.documentation: The AWS Marketplace solution ARNs associated with this opportunity.

AwsMarketplaceProducts.documentation: The AWS Marketplace product ARNs associated with this opportunity.

AwsOpportunityRelatedEntities.documentation: Represents other entities related to the AWS opportunity, such as AWS products, partner solutions, and marketplace offers. These associations help build a complete picture of the solution being sold.

AwsOpportunityStage.documentation: The stage of an AWS opportunity in its lifecycle.

InvolvementType.documentation: Type of AWS involvement in the opportunity.

LifeCycle.documentation: Contains lifecycle details of the AWS opportunity, such as its stage, review status, and target close date.

OpportunityTeam.documentation: AWS team members involved in the opportunity.

Insights.documentation: Contains the insights that AWS provides for the opportunity, such as the engagement score and the recommended next actions.

InvolvementTypeChangeReason.documentation: Reason for changes in AWS involvement type for the opportunity.

RelatedEntityIds.documentation: Lists the identifiers of entities that relate to the AWS opportunity, such as AWS products and partner solutions.

Customer.documentation: Contains details about the customer that the AWS opportunity belongs to.

Project.documentation: Contains details about the project that the AWS opportunity covers.

CosellMotion.documentation: Engagement classification for this opportunity. Read-only. Null before scoring. Known values: AWS Field-engaged, Agent-engaged, Partner-led.

CosellMotionReason.documentation: The plain-language reason for the current CosellMotion value. Read-only. Null when CosellMotion is null.

SoftwareRevenue.documentation: Seller-provided PARC deal terms: commitment value, discount, and contract dates.

AwsOpportunitySummaryFullView.documentation: Provides a comprehensive view of AwsOpportunitySummaryFullView template.

AwsOpportunityTeamMembersList.documentation: A list of AWS team members who work on the opportunity.

AwsPartition.documentation: The AWS partition where the opportunity will run. A partition is a group of AWS Regions with its own endpoints and IAM configuration. The only value is aws-eusc, which stands for the AWS European Sovereign Cloud.

ProductCode.documentation: AWS Partner Central product identifier used for opportunity association.

Categories.documentation: List of program and pathway categories this product is eligible for.

Optimizations.documentation: List of specific optimization recommendations for this product.

AwsProductDetails.documentation: List of AWS services with program eligibility indicators (MAP, modernization pathways), cost estimates, and optimization recommendations.

CurrencyCode.documentation: ISO 4217 currency code. Supported values are USD and EUR. Returns EUR when the opportunity is in the aws-eusc (AWS European Sovereign Cloud) partition.

TotalAmount.documentation: Total estimated spend for this source before optimizations.

TotalOptimizedAmount.documentation: Total estimated spend after applying recommended optimizations.

TotalAmountByCategory.documentation: Spend amounts mapped to AWS programs and modernization pathways.

AwsProducts.documentation: Product-level details including costs and optimization recommendations.

AwsProductInsights.documentation: Comprehensive spend analysis for a single source (AWS or Partner) including total amounts, optimization savings, program category breakdowns, and detailed product-level insights.

SavingsAmount.documentation: Quantified cost savings achievable by implementing this optimization.

AwsProductOptimization.documentation: Specific optimization strategies partners can implement to reduce costs.

AwsProductsList.documentation: List of AWS services with program eligibility indicators.

Partner.documentation: Partner-sourced insights derived from Pricing Calculator URLs.

AWS.documentation: AI-generated insights including recommended products from AWS.

AwsProductsSpendInsightsBySource.documentation: Source-separated spend insights that provide independent analysis for AWS recommendations and partner estimates.

Value.documentation: The committed value and currency for the procurement terms.

Discount.documentation: Discount percentage offered on the software revenue. Percent convention: 15.00 means 15%.

AwsSoftwareRevenue.documentation: Seller-provided PARC deal terms for the opportunity, including commitment value, discount percentage, and contract dates.

InvolvementType.documentation: Specifies the type of AWS involvement in the opportunity, such as coselling, deal support, or technical consultation. This helps categorize the nature of AWS participation.

Visibility.documentation: Determines who can view AWS involvement in the opportunity. Typically, this field is set to Full for most cases, but it may be restricted based on special program requirements or confidentiality needs.

AwsSubmission.documentation: Indicates the level of AWS involvement in the opportunity. This field helps track AWS participation throughout the engagement, such as providing technical support, deal assistance, and sales support.

Email.documentation: Provides the Amazon Web Services team member's email address.

FirstName.documentation: Provides the Amazon Web Services team member's first name.

LastName.documentation: Provides the Amazon Web Services team member's last name.

BusinessTitle.documentation: Specifies the Amazon Web Services team member's business title and indicates their organizational role.

AwsTeamMember.documentation: Represents an Amazon Web Services team member for the engagement. This structure includes details such as name, email, and business title.

AwsTeamMemberFirstNameString.documentation: The name of a person or a company.

AwsTeamMemberLastNameString.documentation: The name of a person or a company.

Day.documentation: The day of the week that this outreach window applies to. Valid values are MONDAY, TUESDAY, WEDNESDAY, THURSDAY, FRIDAY, SATURDAY, and SUNDAY.

StartTimeUtc.documentation: The inclusive start of the outreach window, in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC), in 24-hour HH:mm format.

EndTimeUtc.documentation: The exclusive end of the outreach window, in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC), in 24-hour HH:mm format.

BestOutreachWindow.documentation: A single recommended outreach window for one day, expressed in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC).

BestOutreachWindowList.documentation: One to seven distinct complete outreach windows. Multiple windows may use the same day.

Values.documentation: The field value that defines this group.

Count.documentation: The number of customer accounts in this group.

Bucket.documentation: One group in an aggregation result. It includes the field values that define the group and the number of customer accounts in it.

BulkFileFormat.documentation: File format for bulk input and report files.

BulkFileName.documentation: Display name of the uploaded file (derived from the job's file URI), surfaced in responses so a partner can recognise a job by the file they uploaded rather than the random JobId.

BulkJobArnOrIdentifier.documentation: Information about bulk job arn or identifier.

RequestId.documentation: The identifier of the record in the bulk job file.

Status.documentation: The outcome of processing the record.

ResourceIdentifier.documentation: This value is the identifier of the resource that Partner Central created or updated for the record. A failed record includes this value when Partner Central created the resource before the failure.

ErrorCode.documentation: A code that identifies why the record failed. Present only when the record failed.

ErrorMessage.documentation: A description of why the record failed. Present only when the record failed.

BulkJobResult.documentation: The outcome of processing a single record within a bulk job. It identifies the record and, when the record didn't succeed, carries an error code and message.

BulkOperationType.documentation: The operation a bulk job performs on each record, determined by the template the partner uploads: BULK_CREATE creates new records, BULK_UPDATE updates existing ones.

BulkRecordStatus.documentation: Outcome status for a single record in a bulk job.

BulkReportUrl.documentation: Short-lived presigned URL for downloading a report file.

Channel.documentation: A marketing channel that the partner uses for a marketing activity.

RecommendedChannel.documentation: The recommended outreach channel for the group of similar leads. Valid values are EMAIL and CALL.

BestOutreachWindows.documentation: The recommended day-specific outreach windows for the recommended channel, expressed in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC). Each window applies to one day, and more than one window can fall on the same day. This field is optional and appears only when window guidance is available.

ChannelRecommendation.documentation: Aggregated outreach guidance for leads that share the same country, geography, region, and company segment. It names the outreach channel most commonly recommended for that group and, optionally, the days and times that channel is best used. This is group-level guidance. It doesn't describe an individual lead's contact history or rank recommendations for a specific lead.

Channels.documentation: A list of marketing channels that the partner uses for a marketing activity.

ClientToken.documentation: A unique, case-sensitive identifier that the client provides to make a request idempotent.

ClosedLostReason.documentation: The reason that the partner gives for closing an opportunity as lost.

CompetitorName.documentation: The name of a competitor of the opportunity.

This error occurs when the request can’t be processed due to a conflict with the target resource's current state, which could result from updating or deleting the resource.

Suggested action: Fetch the latest state of the resource, verify the state, and retry the request.

Email.documentation: The contact's email address associated with the Opportunity.

FirstName.documentation: The contact's first name associated with the Opportunity.

LastName.documentation: The contact's last name associated with the Opportunity.

BusinessTitle.documentation: The partner contact's title (job title or role) associated with the Opportunity. BusinessTitle supports either PartnerAccountManager or OpportunityOwner.

Phone.documentation: The contact's phone number associated with the Opportunity.

Contact.documentation: An object that contains a Customer Partner's contact details.

ContactFirstNameString.documentation: The name of a person or a company.

ContactLastNameString.documentation: The name of a person or a company.

ContactWindow.documentation: A part of the day when a contact prefers to be reached. Valid values are MORNING, AFTERNOON, and EVENING.

ContextIdentifier.documentation: The identifier of an engagement context. The value is a whole number that doesn't start with zero.

CosellMotion.documentation: The engagement classification of an AWS opportunity, such as AWS Field-engaged, Agent-engaged, or Partner-led.
