Specifies the catalog for the request. Valid values:

  • AWS: Production.

  • Sandbox: Testing environments.

Account.documentation: Specifies the details of the customer, such as the company name, website, and address. AWS uses these details to match the account to a customer.

PartnerAccountIdentifier.documentation: Specifies your own identifier for the customer account, such as the account ID in your CRM system. Use it to correlate the customer account with your records.

Tags.documentation: Specifies the tags to add to the customer account. Each tag is a key-value pair.

ClientToken.documentation: Specifies a unique, case-sensitive identifier that you provide to make the request idempotent. If you retry a request with the same token, the operation returns the result of the original request instead of creating another customer account.

Arn.documentation: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the customer account.

Id.documentation: The unique identifier of the customer account.

Status.documentation: The enrichment status of the new customer account. A new account starts as PENDING.

Catalog.documentation: The catalog that the customer account belongs to.

PartnerAccountIdentifier.documentation: Your own identifier for the customer account, if you provided one.

CreatedDate.documentation: The date and time when the customer account was created.

Catalog.documentation: Specifies the catalog associated with the engagement context request. This field takes a string value from a predefined list: AWS or Sandbox. The catalog determines which environment the engagement context is created in. Use AWS to create contexts in the production environment, and Sandbox for testing in secure, isolated environments.

EngagementIdentifier.documentation: The unique identifier of the Engagement for which the context is being created. This parameter ensures the context is associated with the correct engagement and provides the necessary linkage between the engagement and its contextual information.

ClientToken.documentation: A unique, case-sensitive identifier provided by the client to ensure that the request is handled exactly once. This token helps prevent duplicate context creations and must not exceed sixty-four alphanumeric characters. Use a UUID or other unique string to ensure idempotency.

Type.documentation: Specifies the type of context being created for the engagement. This field determines the structure and content of the context payload. Valid values include CustomerProject for customer project-related contexts. The type field ensures that the context is properly categorized and processed according to its intended purpose.

Payload.documentation: Contains the contextual information to add to the engagement. The structure of this payload depends on the context type in the Type field.

CreateEngagementContextRequest.documentation: Contains the request parameters for the CreateEngagementContext operation.

EngagementId.documentation: The unique identifier of the engagement to which the context was added. This ID confirms the successful association of the context with the specified engagement.

EngagementArn.documentation: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the engagement to which the context was added. This globally unique identifier can be used for cross-service references and IAM policies.

EngagementLastModifiedAt.documentation: The timestamp indicating when the engagement was last modified as a result of adding the context, in ISO 8601 format (UTC). Example: "2023-05-01T20:37:46Z".

ContextId.documentation: The unique identifier assigned to the newly created engagement context. This ID can be used to reference the specific context within the engagement for future operations.

CreateEngagementContextResponse.documentation: Contains the response that the CreateEngagementContext action returns.

Catalog.documentation: Specifies the catalog related to the engagement. Accepted values are AWS and Sandbox, which determine the environment in which the engagement is managed.

ClientToken.documentation: Specifies a unique, client-generated UUID to ensure that the request is handled exactly once. This token helps prevent duplicate invitation creations.

EngagementIdentifier.documentation: The unique identifier of the Engagement associated with the invitation. This parameter ensures the invitation is created within the correct Engagement context.

Invitation.documentation: The Invitation object all information necessary to initiate an engagement invitation to a partner. It contains a personalized message from the sender, the invitation's receiver, and a payload. The Payload can be the OpportunityInvitation, which includes detailed structures for sender contacts, partner responsibilities, customer information, and project details, or LeadInvitation, which includes structures for customer information and interaction details.

CreateEngagementInvitationRequest.documentation: Contains the request parameters for the CreateEngagementInvitation operation.

Id.documentation: Unique identifier assigned to the newly created engagement invitation.

Arn.documentation: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the engagement invitation.

CreateEngagementInvitationResponse.documentation: Contains the response that the CreateEngagementInvitation action returns.

Catalog.documentation: The CreateEngagementRequest$Catalog parameter specifies the catalog related to the engagement. Accepted values are AWS and Sandbox, which determine the environment in which the engagement is managed.

ClientToken.documentation: The CreateEngagementRequest$ClientToken parameter specifies a unique, case-sensitive identifier to ensure that the request is handled exactly once. The value must not exceed sixty-four alphanumeric characters.

Contexts.documentation: The Contexts field is a required array of objects, with a maximum of 5 contexts allowed, specifying detailed information about customer projects associated with the Engagement. Each context object contains a Type field indicating the context type, which must be CustomerProject in this version, and a Payload field containing the CustomerProject details. The CustomerProject object is composed of two main components: Customer and Project. The Customer object includes information such as CompanyName, WebsiteUrl, Industry, and CountryCode, providing essential details about the customer. The Project object contains Title, BusinessProblem, and TargetCompletionDate, offering insights into the specific project associated with the customer. This structure allows comprehensive context to be included within the Engagement, facilitating effective collaboration between parties by providing relevant customer and project information.

CreateEngagementRequest.documentation: Contains the request parameters for the CreateEngagement operation.

Id.documentation: Unique identifier assigned to the newly created engagement.

Arn.documentation: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that identifies the engagement.

ModifiedAt.documentation: The timestamp indicating when the engagement was last modified, in ISO 8601 format (UTC). For newly created engagements, this value matches the creation timestamp. Example: "2023-05-01T20:37:46Z".

CreateEngagementResponse.documentation: Contains the response that the CreateEngagement action returns.

Catalog.documentation: Specifies the catalog associated with the request. This field takes a string value from a predefined list: AWS or Sandbox. The catalog determines which environment the opportunity is created in. Use AWS to create opportunities in the Amazon Web Services catalog, and Sandbox for testing in secure, isolated environments.

PrimaryNeedsFromAws.documentation:
Identifies the type of support the partner needs from Amazon Web Services.

Valid values:

  • Cosell—Architectural Validation: Confirmation from Amazon Web Services that the partner's proposed solution architecture is aligned with Amazon Web Services best practices and poses minimal architectural risks.

  • Cosell—Business Presentation: Request Amazon Web Services seller's participation in a joint customer presentation.

  • Cosell—Competitive Information: Access to Amazon Web Services competitive resources and support for the partner's proposed solution.

  • Cosell—Pricing Assistance: Connect with an Amazon Web Services seller for support situations where a partner may be receiving an upfront discount on a service (for example: EDP deals).

  • Cosell—Technical Consultation: Connect with an Amazon Web Services Solutions Architect to address the partner's questions about the proposed solution.

  • Cosell—Total Cost of Ownership Evaluation: Assistance with quoting different cost savings of proposed solutions on Amazon Web Services versus on-premises or a traditional hosting environment.

  • Cosell—Deal Support: Request Amazon Web Services seller's support to progress the opportunity (for example: joint customer call, strategic positioning).

  • Cosell—Support for Public Tender/RFx: Opportunity related to the public sector where the partner needs Amazon Web Services RFx support.

NationalSecurity.documentation: Indicates whether the Opportunity pertains to a national security project. This field must be set to true only when the customer's industry is Government. Additional privacy and security measures apply during the review and management process for opportunities marked as NationalSecurity.

PartnerOpportunityIdentifier.documentation:
Specifies the opportunity's unique identifier in the partner's CRM system. This value is essential to track and reconcile because it's included in the outbound payload to the partner.

This field allows partners to link an opportunity to their CRM, which helps to ensure seamless integration and accurate synchronization between the Partner Central API and the partner's internal systems.

Customer.documentation: Specifies customer details associated with the Opportunity.

Project.documentation: An object that contains project details for the Opportunity.

OpportunityType.documentation:
Specifies the opportunity type as a renewal, new, or expansion.

Opportunity types:

  • New opportunity: Represents a new business opportunity with a potential customer that's not previously engaged with your solutions or services.

  • Renewal opportunity: Represents an opportunity to renew an existing contract or subscription with a current customer, ensuring continuity of service.

  • Expansion opportunity: Represents an opportunity to expand the scope of an existing contract or subscription, either by adding new services or increasing the volume of existing services for a current customer.

Marketing.documentation: This object contains marketing details and is optional for an opportunity.

SoftwareRevenue.documentation: Specifies details of a customer's procurement terms. This is required only for partners in eligible programs.

ClientToken.documentation:
Required to be unique, and should be unchanging, it can be randomly generated or a meaningful string.

Default: None

Best practice: To help ensure uniqueness and avoid conflicts, use a Universally Unique Identifier (UUID) as the ClientToken. You can use standard libraries from most programming languages to generate this. If you use the same client token, the API returns the following error: "Conflicting client token submitted for a new request body."

LifeCycle.documentation: An object that contains lifecycle details for the Opportunity.

Origin.documentation: Specifies the origin of the opportunity, indicating if it was sourced from Amazon Web Services or the partner. For all opportunities created with Catalog: AWS, this field must only be Partner Referral. However, when using Catalog: Sandbox, you can set this field to AWS Referral to simulate Amazon Web Services referral creation. This allows Amazon Web Services-originated flows testing in the sandbox catalog.

OpportunityTeam.documentation: Represents the internal team handling the opportunity. Specify collaborating members of this opportunity who are within the partner's organization.

Tags.documentation: A map of the key-value pairs of the tag or tags to assign.

CreateOpportunityRequest.documentation: Contains the request parameters for the CreateOpportunity operation.

Id.documentation: Read-only, system-generated Opportunity unique identifier. Amazon Web Services creates this identifier, and it's used for all subsequent opportunity actions, such as updates, associations, and submissions. It helps to ensure that each opportunity is accurately tracked and managed.

PartnerOpportunityIdentifier.documentation: Specifies the opportunity's unique identifier in the partner's CRM system. This value is essential to track and reconcile because it's included in the outbound payload sent back to the partner.

LastModifiedDate.documentation: DateTime when the opportunity was last modified. When the Opportunity is created, its value is CreatedDate.

CreateOpportunityResponse.documentation: Contains the response that the CreateOpportunity action returns.

Catalog.documentation: Specifies the catalog in which to create the snapshot job. Valid values are AWS and Sandbox.

ClientToken.documentation: A client-generated UUID used for idempotency check. The token helps prevent duplicate job creations.

EngagementIdentifier.documentation: Specifies the identifier of the engagement associated with the resource to be snapshotted.

ResourceType.documentation: The type of resource for which the snapshot job is being created. Must be one of the supported resource types i.e. Opportunity

ResourceIdentifier.documentation: Specifies the identifier of the specific resource to be snapshotted. The format depends on the ResourceType.

ResourceSnapshotTemplateIdentifier.documentation: Specifies the name of the template that defines the schema for the snapshot.

Tags.documentation: A map of the key-value pairs of the tag or tags to assign.

CreateResourceSnapshotJobRequest.documentation: Contains the request parameters for the CreateResourceSnapshotJob operation.

Id.documentation: The unique identifier for the created snapshot job.

Arn.documentation: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the created snapshot job.

CreateResourceSnapshotJobResponse.documentation: Contains the response that the CreateResourceSnapshotJob action returns.

Catalog.documentation: Specifies the catalog where the snapshot is created. Valid values are AWS and Sandbox.

EngagementIdentifier.documentation: The unique identifier of the engagement associated with this snapshot. This field links the snapshot to a specific engagement context.

ResourceType.documentation: Specifies the type of resource for which the snapshot is being created. This field determines the structure and content of the snapshot. Must be one of the supported resource types, such as: Opportunity.

ResourceIdentifier.documentation: The unique identifier of the specific resource to be snapshotted. The format and constraints of this identifier depend on the ResourceType specified. For example: For Opportunity type, it will be an opportunity ID.

ResourceSnapshotTemplateIdentifier.documentation: The name of the template that defines the schema for the snapshot. This template determines which subset of the resource data will be included in the snapshot. Must correspond to an existing and valid template for the specified ResourceType.

ClientToken.documentation: Specifies a unique, client-generated UUID to ensure that the request is handled exactly once. This token helps prevent duplicate snapshot creations.

CreateResourceSnapshotRequest.documentation: Contains the request parameters for the CreateResourceSnapshot operation.

Arn.documentation: Specifies the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the snapshot created.

Revision.documentation: Specifies the revision number of the created snapshot. This field provides important information about the snapshot's place in the sequence of snapshots for the given resource.

CreateResourceSnapshotResponse.documentation: Contains the response that the CreateResourceSnapshot action returns.

CreatedDateFilter.documentation: Filter for opportunities based on creation date range.

CurrencyCode.documentation: A three-letter ISO 4217 currency code, such as USD.

Account.documentation: An object that contains the customer's account details.

Contacts.documentation: Represents the contact details for individuals associated with the customer of the Opportunity. This field captures relevant contacts, including decision-makers, influencers, and technical stakeholders within the customer organization. These contacts are key to progressing the opportunity.

Customer.documentation: An object that contains the customer's Account and Contact.

CustomerAccountArnOrIdentifier.documentation: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) or the identifier of a customer account. An identifier starts with cust-acc- followed by 13 lowercase letters or digits.

Identifier.documentation: Filters the results to the bulk job with the specified ARN or identifier.

Status.documentation: Filters the results to bulk jobs with the specified status.

CustomerAccountBulkJobFilter.documentation: The criteria that limit which bulk jobs ListCustomerAccountBulkJobs returns.

Arn.documentation: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the bulk job.

Id.documentation: The unique identifier of the bulk job.

Status.documentation: The current status of the bulk job.

FileName.documentation: The name of the file that the job processes.

TotalRecords.documentation: The total number of records in the file. The value is 0 until the job reads the file.

ProcessedRecords.documentation: The number of records that the job has finished processing.

SuccessCount.documentation: The number of records that the job processed successfully.

DeletedCount.documentation: The number of accounts imported by this job that have since been deleted. This counter only increases, so the accounts still present equal SuccessCount minus DeletedCount.

FailureReason.documentation: The reason that the job failed. Present only when the job status is FAILED.

CreatedAt.documentation: The date and time when the bulk job was created.

CompletedAt.documentation: The date and time when the job finished. Absent while the job is running.

CustomerAccountBulkJobSummary.documentation: A bulk job in the results of ListCustomerAccountBulkJobs. It includes the job status, the file name, and the record counts.

CustomerAccountBulkJobSummaryList.documentation: Information about customer account bulk job summary list.

AccountIdentifier.documentation: The identifier of the customer account that the engagement concerns, as an Amazon Resource Name (ARN) or a customer account identifier.

Customer.documentation: A snapshot of the customer company's identity for the account. On read, the service populates this from the account identifier.

CustomerAccountContext.documentation: The customer account context for an account-planning engagement. It names the account the plan concerns. The identifying details can be supplied by the caller or derived by the service from the account identifier.

WebsiteUrl.documentation: The website URL of the customer company.

Duns.documentation: The Data Universal Numbering System (DUNS) number of the customer company.

OtherIndustry.documentation: A description of the industry, used when the industry is Other.

Domain.documentation: The internet domain of the customer company, such as example.com.

ParentCompanyName.documentation: The name of the parent company of the customer company, if any.

CustomerAccountData.documentation: The customer information that you provide for a customer account, such as the company name, website, and address. We use these details to match the account to a customer.

CustomerAccountDataCompanyNameString.documentation: The name of a person or a company.

CustomerAccountDataDunsString.documentation: A nine-digit Data Universal Numbering System (DUNS) number that identifies a company.

CustomerAccountDataParentCompanyNameStri.documentation: The name of a person or a company.

CustomerAccountDetailsSummary.documentation: The customer information for an account in search results. It carries a reduced set of fields compared to the full customer information that GetCustomerAccount returns, omitting sensitive fields such as the Data Universal Numbering System (DUNS) number and the street address. To read those fields, use GetCustomerAccount.

CustomerAccountDetailsSummaryCompanyName.documentation: The name of a person or a company.

CustomerAccountFailureReason.documentation: The reason that a customer account needs your action.

SortBy.documentation: The field to sort the results by.

SortOrder.documentation: The direction of the sort, either ascending or descending.

CustomerAccountSort.documentation: The field to sort customer accounts by, and the sort direction.

Arn.documentation: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the customer account.

Id.documentation: The unique identifier of the customer account.

Catalog.documentation: The catalog that the customer account belongs to.

EnrichmentStatus.documentation: The enrichment status of the customer account.

PartnerAccountIdentifier.documentation: Your own identifier for the customer account, if you provided one.

CreatedDate.documentation: The date and time when the customer account was created.

LastModifiedDate.documentation: The date and time when the customer account was last modified.

CustomerAccount.documentation: A summary of the details of the customer that you provided.

AwsEnrichment.documentation: A summary of the enrichment information that AWS provides about the customer. Present only when EnrichmentStatus is ENRICHED.

CustomerAccountSummary.documentation: A customer account in the results of SearchCustomerAccounts. It carries a reduced set of fields compared to the full account that is returned by GetCustomerAccount.

CustomerAccountTagList.documentation: A list of tags to assign to a customer account.

CustomerAction.documentation: An action that the customer took during a lead interaction.

CustomerContactsList.documentation: A list of contacts at the customer's company.

Customer.documentation: Contains details about the customer that the customer project belongs to.

Project.documentation: Information about the customer project associated with the Engagement.

CustomerProjectsContext.documentation:
The CustomerProjects structure in Engagements offers a flexible framework for managing customer-project relationships. It supports multiple customers per Engagement and multiple projects per customer, while also allowing for customers without projects and projects without specific customers.

All Engagement members have full visibility of customers and their associated projects, enabling the capture of relevant context even when project details are not fully defined. This structure also facilitates targeted invitations, allowing partners to focus on specific customers and their business problems when sending Engagement invitations.

Account.documentation: An object that contains a customer's account details.

CustomerSummary.documentation: An object that contains a Customer object's subset of fields.

DateTime.documentation: A date and time in ISO 8601 date-time format, such as 2023-05-01T20:37:46Z.

DayOfWeek.documentation: Days of the week — universally stable set, modeled as enum per API Design Guide.

Catalog.documentation:
Specifies the catalog for the request. Valid values:

  • AWS: Production.

  • Sandbox: Testing environments.

Identifier.documentation: Specifies the ARN or the identifier of the customer account.

Catalog.documentation: Specifies the catalog from which to delete the snapshot job. Valid values are AWS and Sandbox.

ResourceSnapshotJobIdentifier.documentation: The unique identifier of the resource snapshot job to be deleted.

DeleteResourceSnapshotJobRequest.documentation: Contains the request parameters for the DeleteResourceSnapshotJob operation.

DeliveryModel.documentation: A model that the partner uses to deliver the solution to the customer.

DeliveryModels.documentation: A list of models that the partner uses to deliver the solution to the customer.

Catalog.documentation: Specifies the catalog associated with the request. This field takes a string value from a predefined list: AWS or Sandbox. The catalog determines which environment the opportunity disassociation is made in. Use AWS to disassociate opportunities in the Amazon Web Services catalog, and Sandbox for testing in secure, isolated environments.

OpportunityIdentifier.documentation:
The opportunity's unique identifier for when you want to disassociate it from related entities. This identifier helps to ensure that the correct opportunity is updated.

Validation: Ensure that the provided identifier corresponds to an existing opportunity in the Amazon Web Services system because incorrect identifiers result in an error and no changes are made.

RelatedEntityType.documentation:
The type of the entity that you're disassociating from the opportunity. When you specify the entity type, it helps the system correctly process the disassociation request to ensure that the right connections are removed.

Examples of entity types include Partner Solution, Amazon Web Services product, and Amazon Web Services Marketplaceoffer. Ensure that the value matches one of the expected entity types.

Validation: Provide a valid entity type to help ensure successful disassociation. An invalid or incorrect entity type results in an error.

RelatedEntityIdentifier.documentation:
The related entity's identifier that you want to disassociate from the opportunity. Depending on the type of entity, this could be a simple identifier or an Amazon Resource Name (ARN) for entities managed through Amazon Web Services Marketplace.

For Amazon Web Services Marketplace entities, use the Amazon Web Services Marketplace API to obtain the necessary ARNs. For guidance on retrieving these ARNs, see Amazon Web Services MarketplaceUsing the Amazon Web Services Marketplace Catalog API.

Validation: Ensure the identifier or ARN is valid and corresponds to an existing entity. An incorrect or invalid identifier results in an error.

DisassociateOpportunityRequest.documentation: Contains the request parameters for the DisassociateOpportunity operation.

Domain.documentation: The internet domain of a company, such as example.com.

DunsNumber.documentation: A nine-digit Data Universal Numbering System (DUNS) number that identifies a company.

EligibleProgramsList.documentation: A list of AWS Greenfield programs that the prospected customer is eligible for.

EngagementArn.documentation: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that identifies an engagement.

EngagementArnOrIdentifier.documentation: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) or the identifier of an engagement. An identifier starts with eng- followed by 14 lowercase letters or digits.

Id.documentation: The unique identifier of the engagement context. This ID is used to reference and manage the specific context within the engagement.

Type.documentation: Specifies the type of Engagement context. Valid values are "CustomerProject" or "Document", indicating whether the context relates to a customer project or a document respectively.

Payload.documentation: Contains the specific details of the Engagement context. The structure of this payload varies depending on the Type field.

EngagementContextDetails.documentation: Provides detailed context information for an Engagement. This structure allows for specifying the type of context and its associated payload.

CustomerProject.documentation: Contains detailed information about a customer project when the context type is "CustomerProject". This field is present only when the Type in EngagementContextDetails is set to "CustomerProject".

Lead.documentation: Contains detailed information about a lead when the context type is "Lead". This field is present only when the Type in EngagementContextDetails is set to "Lead".

ProspectingResult.documentation: Contains prospecting result data with enriched insights. The system generates these insights when a partner runs an autonomous prospecting job on leads. This field appears only when the context type is "ProspectingResult".

CustomerAccount.documentation: The customer account context for account planning. This field appears only when the context type is CustomerAccount.

EngagementContextPayload.documentation: Represents the payload of an Engagement context. The structure of this payload varies based on the context type specified in the EngagementContextDetails.

EngagementContextType.documentation: The type of an engagement context. Valid values are CustomerProject, Lead, ProspectingResult, and CustomerAccount.

Industry.documentation: Specifies the industry to which the customer’s company belongs. This field helps categorize the opportunity based on the customer’s business sector.

CompanyName.documentation: Represents the name of the customer’s company associated with the Engagement Invitation. This field is used to identify the customer.

WebsiteUrl.documentation: Provides the website URL of the customer’s company. This field helps partners verify the legitimacy and size of the customer organization.

CountryCode.documentation: Indicates the country in which the customer’s company operates. This field is useful for understanding regional requirements or compliance needs.

EngagementCustomer.documentation: Contains details about the customer associated with the Engagement Invitation, including company information and industry.

EngagementCustomerBusinessProblem.documentation: A description of the business problem that the customer wants to solve.

BusinessProblem.documentation: A description of the business problem the project aims to solve.

TargetCompletionDate.documentation: The target completion date for the customer's project.

EngagementCustomerProjectDetails.documentation: Provides comprehensive details about a customer project associated with an Engagement. This may include information such as project goals, timelines, and specific customer requirements.

EngagementCustomerProjectTitle.documentation: The title of the customer project in an engagement.

EngagementGroupArn.documentation: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of an engagement group.

EngagementGroupArnOrIdentifier.documentation:
Specifies an engagement group. You can specify either of the following:

  • An engagement group identifier.

  • An engagement group ARN.

EngagementGroupIdentifiers.documentation: A list of engagement group identifiers or ARNs.

SortBy.documentation: The field to sort the results by.

SortOrder.documentation: The direction of the sort, either ascending or descending.

EngagementGroupSort.documentation: Configures sorting of the engagement groups returned by ListEngagementGroups.

EngagementGroupSortName.documentation: The engagement group fields that you can sort on in ListEngagementGroups.

Id.documentation: The unique identifier of the engagement group. Pass this value to SearchEngagements as GroupId.

Arn.documentation: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the engagement group.

Catalog.documentation: The catalog that the engagement group belongs to.

Description.documentation: A description of the engagements that the group targets.

Count.documentation: The number of engagements in the group that are available to you.

ReadinessLevel.documentation: The readiness level of the engagement group, which indicates the recommended call to action for its leads.

UpdatedAt.documentation: The date and time when the engagement group was last updated, in ISO 8601 format, in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC).

EngagementGroupSummary.documentation: A summary of an engagement group: a curated set of engagements that share common characteristics.

EngagementIdentifier.documentation: The identifier of an engagement. An identifier starts with eng- followed by 14 lowercase letters or digits.

EngagementIdentifiers.documentation: A list of engagement identifiers or Amazon Resource Names (ARNs).

EngagementInvitationArn.documentation: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that identifies an engagement invitation.

EngagementInvitationArnOrIdentifier.documentation: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) or the identifier of an engagement invitation. An identifier starts with engi- followed by 13 lowercase letters or digits.

EngagementInvitationIdentifier.documentation: The identifier of an engagement invitation. An identifier starts with engi- followed by 13 lowercase letters or digits.

EngagementInvitationIdentifiers.documentation: A list of engagement invitation identifiers or Amazon Resource Names (ARNs).

EngagementInvitationPayloadType.documentation: The type of payload that an engagement invitation carries. Valid values are OpportunityInvitation, LeadInvitation, and AccountPlanningInvitation.

EngagementInvitationSummaries.documentation: A list of summaries of engagement invitations.

Arn.documentation: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Engagement Invitation. The ARN is a unique identifier that allows partners to reference the invitation in their system and manage its lifecycle.

PayloadType.documentation: Describes the type of payload associated with the Engagement Invitation, such as Opportunity or MarketplaceOffer. This helps partners understand the nature of the engagement request from AWS.

Id.documentation: Represents the unique identifier of the Engagement Invitation. This identifier is used to track the invitation and to manage responses like acceptance or rejection.

EngagementId.documentation: The identifier of the Engagement associated with this invitation. This links the invitation to its parent Engagement.

EngagementTitle.documentation: Provides a short title or description of the Engagement Invitation. This title helps partners quickly identify and differentiate between multiple engagement opportunities.

Status.documentation: Represents the current status of the Engagement Invitation, such as Pending, Accepted, or Rejected. The status helps track the progress and response to the invitation.

InvitationDate.documentation: Indicates the date when the Engagement Invitation was sent to the partner. This provides context for when the opportunity was shared and helps in tracking the timeline for engagement.

ExpirationDate.documentation: Indicates the date and time when the Engagement Invitation will expire. After this date, the invitation can no longer be accepted, and the opportunity will be unavailable to the partner.

SenderAwsAccountId.documentation: Specifies the AWS account ID of the sender who initiated the Engagement Invitation. This allows the partner to identify the AWS entity or representative responsible for sharing the opportunity.

SenderCompanyName.documentation: Indicates the name of the company or AWS division that sent the Engagement Invitation. This information is useful for partners to know which part of AWS is requesting engagement.

Receiver.documentation: Specifies the partner company or individual that received the Engagement Invitation. This field is important for tracking who the invitation was sent to within the partner organization.

Catalog.documentation: Specifies the catalog in which the Engagement Invitation resides. This can be either the AWS or Sandbox catalog, indicating whether the opportunity is live or being tested.

ParticipantType.documentation: Identifies the role of the caller in the engagement invitation.

EngagementInvitationSummary.documentation: Provides a summarized view of the Engagement Invitation, including details like the identifier, status, and sender. This summary helps partners track and manage AWS originated opportunities.

EngagementInvitationsPayloadType.documentation: A list of engagement invitation payload types.

CompanyName.documentation: The official name of the member's company or organization.

WebsiteUrl.documentation: The URL of the member company's website. This offers a way to find more information about the member organization and serves as an additional identifier.

AccountId.documentation: This is the unique identifier for the AWS account associated with the member organization. It's used for AWS-related operations and identity verification.

EngagementMember.documentation:
Engagement members are the participants in an Engagement, which is likely a collaborative project or business opportunity within the AWS partner network. Members can be different partner organizations or AWS accounts that are working together on a specific engagement.

Each member is represented by their AWS Account ID, Company Name, and associated details. Members have a status within the Engagement (PENDING, ACCEPTED, REJECTED, or WITHDRAWN), indicating their current state of participation. Only existing members of an Engagement can view the list of other members. This implies a level of privacy and access control within the Engagement structure.

EngagementMemberSummaries.documentation: A list of summaries of engagement members.

CompanyName.documentation: The official name of the member's company or organization.

WebsiteUrl.documentation: The URL of the member company's website. This offers a way to find more information about the member organization and serves as an additional identifier.

EngagementMemberSummary.documentation: The EngagementMemberSummary provides a snapshot of essential information about participants in an AWS Partner Central Engagement. This compact data structure encapsulates key details of each member, facilitating efficient collaboration and management within the Engagement.

EngagementPageSize.documentation: The maximum number of engagements that a single call returns. The default is 20. Valid values range from 1 to 100.

EngagementIdentifier.documentation: The unique identifier of the engagement that was processed.

EngagementContextId.documentation: The identifier of the prospecting context created for this engagement. This field is only populated when the engagement was processed successfully (status is COMPLETED). Use this identifier to reference the prospecting context in subsequent operations.

Status.documentation: The processing status of this specific engagement. Possible values are PENDING, IN_PROGRESS, COMPLETED, and FAILED.

ReasonCode.documentation: An enumerated code indicating the reason this engagement failed to process. This field is only populated when Status is FAILED.

Message.documentation: A human-readable description of the failure for this engagement, including suggested recovery steps. This field is only populated when Status is FAILED.

EngagementProspectingResult.documentation: Contains the result of processing a single engagement within a prospecting task. Each engagement is processed independently, so individual engagements can succeed or fail regardless of other engagements in the same task.

EngagementProspectingResultList.documentation: A list of engagements that contain prospecting results.

Catalog.documentation: Indicates the environment in which the resource and engagement exist.

EngagementId.documentation: A unique identifier for the engagement associated with the resource.

ResourceType.documentation: Categorizes the type of resource associated with the engagement.

ResourceId.documentation: A unique identifier for the specific resource. Varies depending on the resource type.

CreatedBy.documentation: The AWS account ID of the entity that owns the resource. Identifies the account responsible for or having primary control over the resource.

EngagementResourceAssociationSummary.documentation: This provide a streamlined view of the relationships between engagements and resources. These summaries offer a crucial link between collaborative engagements and the specific resources involved, such as opportunities.These summaries are particularly valuable for partners navigating complex engagements with multiple resources. They enable quick insights into resource distribution across engagements, support efficient resource management, and help maintain a clear overview of collaborative activities.

EngagementResourceAssociationSummaryList.documentation: A list of summaries of resources that are associated with an engagement.

EngagementScore.documentation: A score that AWS assigns to show how likely an opportunity is to succeed. Valid values are High, Medium, and Low.

EngagementScoreLevel.documentation: The level of engagement that the prospected customer has with AWS Marketplace. Valid values are High, Medium, and Low.

AndAllFilters.documentation: A list of sub-filters that are joined with a logical AND. The node matches only when every sub-filter matches.

OrAllFilters.documentation: A list of sub-filters that are joined with a logical OR. The node matches when at least one sub-filter matches.

NotFilter.documentation: A single sub-filter that is negated. The node matches when the sub-filter does not match.

EqualsTo.documentation: A leaf condition that matches when the field equals the supplied StringValue.

ContainsAny.documentation: A leaf condition that matches when the field contains any of the supplied values as a case-insensitive substring. Specify a single StringValue or a StringListValue. For a field that holds one value for each lead interaction, the condition matches when any of those values contains a supplied value. Supported on string fields only.

ContainsAll.documentation: A leaf condition that matches when the field holds every supplied value exactly. Specify a single StringValue or a StringListValue. For a field that holds one value for each lead interaction, each supplied value must be present on at least one interaction. For a single-valued field, a list of more than one value returns no results. Supported on string fields only.

GreaterThan.documentation: A leaf condition that matches when the field is greater than the supplied value. This condition is supported only on ordered fields, such as date and numeric fields.

GreaterThanOrEquals.documentation: A leaf condition that matches when the field is greater than or equal to the supplied value. This condition is supported only on ordered fields, such as date and numeric fields.

LessThan.documentation: A leaf condition that matches when the field is less than the supplied value. This condition is supported only on ordered fields, such as date and numeric fields.

LessThanOrEquals.documentation: A leaf condition that matches when the field is less than or equal to the supplied value. This condition is supported only on ordered fields, such as date and numeric fields.

EngagementSearchFilter.documentation: A recursive filter node. Exactly one member must be set. The boolean combinators nest sub-filters: AndAllFilters joins its children with AND, OrAllFilters matches when at least one child matches, and NotFilter negates its single child. The remaining members are leaf conditions over a single field. Nesting is limited to a depth of 3, and each combinator list can contain up to 10 entries.

EngagementSearchFilterList.documentation: A list of filter nodes combined by a boolean combinator.

EngagementSearchFilterName.documentation: The engagement fields that you can filter on in SearchEngagements.

StringValue.documentation: A single string value, used by EqualsTo, ContainsAny, and ContainsAll.

StringListValue.documentation: A list of 1 to 20 string values, used by ContainsAny and ContainsAll.

LongValue.documentation: An integral numeric value, used by the range comparisons on numeric fields.

DateValue.documentation: A date-time value in RFC 3339 format, used by the range comparisons on date fields.

EngagementSearchFilterValue.documentation:
The value that a leaf condition compares against. Specify one of the following:

  • StringValue: A single string, used with EqualsTo, ContainsAny, and ContainsAll.

  • StringListValue: A list of strings, used with ContainsAny and ContainsAll.

  • DateValue: A date and time, used with range comparisons on date fields.

  • LongValue: A whole number, used with range comparisons on numeric fields.

EngagementSearchFilterValues.documentation: A list of 1 to 20 string values, used by ContainsAny and ContainsAll.

EngagementSearchKeyword.documentation: A free-text search term matched against the engagement fields.

Key.documentation: The engagement field that the condition applies to.

Value.documentation: The typed value the condition compares against.

EngagementSearchPredicate.documentation: A leaf condition in an EngagementSearchFilter tree. It specifies the field (Key) and the typed value (Value) to compare. The EngagementSearchFilter member that contains the condition specifies the comparison operator.

SortBy.documentation: The field to sort the results by.

SortOrder.documentation: The direction of the sort, either ascending or descending.

EngagementSearchSortName.documentation: The engagement fields that you can sort on in SearchEngagements. Text and score fields sort in lexical (string) order.

EngagementSearchStringValue.documentation: A string value used in a filter condition.

Id.documentation: The unique resource identifier of the engagement.

Arn.documentation: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the engagement.

CreatedAt.documentation: The date and time when the engagement was created, in ISO 8601 format, in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC).

CreatedBy.documentation: The AWS account ID of the user who created the engagement.

MemberCount.documentation: The number of members in the engagement.

ModifiedAt.documentation: The date and time when the engagement was last modified, in ISO 8601 format, in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC).

ModifiedBy.documentation: The AWS account ID of the user who last modified the engagement.

Contexts.documentation: The contexts associated with the engagement, such as prospecting results, lead details, and customer project details.

EngagementSearchSummary.documentation: A summary of an engagement returned by SearchEngagements. It contains the same engagement fields as the GetEngagement response.

SortOrder.documentation: The order in which to sort the results.

SortBy.documentation: The field by which to sort the results.

EngagementSort.documentation: Specifies the sorting parameters for listing Engagements.

EngagementSortName.documentation: The name of the field that sorts a list of engagements. The only valid value is CreatedDate.

Arn.documentation: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the created Engagement.

Id.documentation: The unique identifier for the Engagement.

CreatedAt.documentation: The date and time when the Engagement was created.

CreatedBy.documentation: The AWS Account ID of the Engagement creator.

MemberCount.documentation: The number of members in the Engagement.

ModifiedAt.documentation: The timestamp indicating when the engagement was last modified, in ISO 8601 format (UTC). Example: "2023-05-01T20:37:46Z".

ModifiedBy.documentation: The AWS account ID of the user who last modified the engagement. This field helps track who made the most recent changes to the engagement.

ContextTypes.documentation: An array of context types associated with the engagement, such as "CustomerProject" or "Lead". This provides a quick overview of the types of contexts included in the engagement.

EngagementSummary.documentation: An object that contains an Engagement's subset of fields.

EngagementUseCase.documentation: The use case that a lead interaction relates to.

ProspectingResultAws.documentation: The customer account data and propensity insights for the prospected account. It includes geographic, industry, and segment classifications, along with engagement and solution scoring.

LeadInsights.documentation: The AI-generated lead readiness score for this lead. Use this score to assess lead quality and prioritize engagement efforts.

EnrichmentContext.documentation: Contains enrichment data for engagement invitations. You can view propensity scores, program eligibility, and lead readiness insights directly in the invitation, before you take action on the invitation.

EnrichmentStatus.documentation: The enrichment status of a customer account.

EstimationUrl.documentation: A URL that points to an estimate in the AWS Pricing Calculator.

Term.documentation: The unit of measurement for the contract duration value. Currently accepts only Months.

Value.documentation: A String representation of the contract duration as an integer, expressed in the unit defined by Term. Valid values range from 1 to 144.

ExpectedContractDuration.documentation: The expected duration of a partner's contract with the customer. Used to convert Total Contract Value (TCV) to Monthly Recurring Revenue (MRR) for opportunity dealsizing calculations.

ExpectedContractDurationTerm.documentation: The unit of measurement for the contract duration value. Currently accepts only Months.

Amount.documentation: Represents the estimated monthly revenue that the partner expects to earn from the opportunity. This helps in forecasting financial returns.

CurrencyCode.documentation: Indicates the currency in which the revenue estimate is provided. This helps in understanding the financial impact across different markets. Accepted values are USD (US Dollars) and EUR (Euros). If the AWS Partition is aws-eusc (AWS European Sovereign Cloud), the currency code must be EUR.

Frequency.documentation: Indicates how frequently the customer is expected to spend the projected amount. Use Monthly for recurring monthly spend (required for TargetCompany: "AWS" entries). Use None for one-time deal value entries (required for TargetCompany: "Self" entries when providing Total Contract Value).

TargetCompany.documentation: Specifies the entity associated with this spend entry. Use AWS for the system’s AWS Monthly Recurring Revenue (MRR) estimate. Use Self for the partner’s own deal value entry when providing Total Contract Value (TCV) for automatic MRR conversion. When ExpectedContractDuration is present on the Project, only AWS and Self are accepted. When ExpectedContractDuration is not present, only AWS is accepted and any other value will be automatically set to AWS.

EstimationUrl.documentation: A URL providing additional information or context about the spend estimation.

ExpectedCustomerSpend.documentation: Provides an estimate of the revenue that the partner is expected to generate from the opportunity. This information helps partners assess the financial value of the project.

ExpectedCustomerSpendList.documentation: A list of the amounts that you expect the customer to spend on the project.

FileUri.documentation: URI pointing to the input file (S3 or HTTPS).

AndAllFilters.documentation: A list of child filters joined with a logical AND. The node matches only when every child filter matches.

OrAllFilters.documentation: A list of child filters joined with a logical OR. The node matches when at least one child filter matches.

NotFilter.documentation: A single child filter that is negated. The node matches when the child filter doesn't match.

EqualsTo.documentation: A condition that matches when the field equals the supplied StringValue.

ContainsAny.documentation: A condition that matches when the field matches any of the values in the supplied StringListValue.

ContainsAll.documentation: A condition that matches when the field contains every value in the supplied StringListValue. Supported on fields that hold more than one value.

GreaterThan.documentation: A condition that matches when the date field is later than the supplied DateValue.

GreaterThanOrEquals.documentation: A condition that matches when the date field is the same as or later than the supplied DateValue.

LessThan.documentation: A condition that matches when the date field is earlier than the supplied DateValue.

LessThanOrEquals.documentation: A condition that matches when the date field is the same as or earlier than the supplied DateValue.

Filter.documentation: A filter node. Specify exactly one member. AndAllFilters, OrAllFilters, and NotFilter combine child filters. The other members compare a single field to a value. Each combinator list can contain up to 10 filters.

Key.documentation: The field that the condition applies to.

Value.documentation: The value that the condition compares the field against.

FilterCondition.documentation: A single comparison in a filter. It names the field to compare and the value to compare it against.

StringListValue.documentation: A list of 1 to 20 string values, used by ContainsAny and ContainsAll.

DateValue.documentation: A date and time value, used by the range comparisons on date fields.

FilterValue.documentation: Specifies the value that a filter compares a field against. This structure holds a single comparison value. Set the member that matches the type of the field you're filtering on.

FilterableField.documentation: The fields that you can filter customer accounts on.

Catalog.documentation: Specifies the catalog in which the AWS Opportunity is located. Accepted values include AWS for production opportunities or Sandbox for testing purposes. The catalog determines which environment the opportunity data is pulled from.

RelatedOpportunityIdentifier.documentation: The unique identifier for the related partner opportunity. Use this field to correlate an AWS opportunity with its corresponding partner opportunity.

GetAwsOpportunitySummaryRequest.documentation: Contains the request parameters for the GetAwsOpportunitySummary operation.

RelatedOpportunityId.documentation: Provides the unique identifier of the related partner opportunity, allowing partners to link the AWS Opportunity to their corresponding opportunity in their CRM system.

Origin.documentation: Specifies whether the AWS Opportunity originated from AWS or the partner. This helps distinguish between opportunities that were sourced by AWS and those referred by the partner.

InvolvementType.documentation: Specifies the type of involvement AWS has in the opportunity, such as direct cosell or advisory support. This field helps partners understand the role AWS plays in advancing the opportunity.

Visibility.documentation: Defines the visibility level for the AWS Opportunity. Use Full visibility for most cases, while Limited visibility is reserved for special programs or sensitive opportunities.

LifeCycle.documentation: Contains lifecycle information for the AWS Opportunity, including review status, stage, and target close date. This field is crucial for partners to monitor the progression of the opportunity.

OpportunityTeam.documentation: Details the AWS opportunity team, including members involved. This information helps partners know who from AWS is engaged and what their role is.

Insights.documentation: Provides insights into the AWS Opportunity, including engagement score and recommended actions that AWS suggests for the partner.

InvolvementTypeChangeReason.documentation: Provides a reason for any changes in the involvement type of AWS in the opportunity. This field is used to track why the level of AWS engagement has changed from For Visibility Only to Co-sell offering transparency into the partnership dynamics.

RelatedEntityIds.documentation: Lists related entity identifiers, such as AWS products or partner solutions, associated with the AWS Opportunity. These identifiers provide additional context and help partners understand which AWS services are involved.

Customer.documentation: Provides details about the customer associated with the AWS Opportunity, including account information, industry, and other customer data. These details help partners understand the business context of the opportunity.

Project.documentation: Provides details about the project associated with the AWS Opportunity, including the customer’s business problem, expected outcomes, and project scope. This information is crucial for understanding the broader context of the opportunity.

CosellMotion.documentation: Engagement classification for this opportunity. Read-only. Null before scoring. Known values: AWS Field-engaged, Agent-engaged, Partner-led.

CosellMotionReason.documentation: The plain-language reason for the current CosellMotion value. Read-only. Null when CosellMotion is null.

SoftwareRevenue.documentation: Seller-provided PARC deal terms: commitment value, discount, and contract dates.

Catalog.documentation: Specifies the catalog in which the AWS Opportunity exists. This is the environment (e.g., AWS or Sandbox) where the opportunity is being managed.

GetAwsOpportunitySummaryResponse.documentation: Contains the response that the GetAwsOpportunitySummary action returns.

Catalog.documentation:
Specifies the catalog for the request. Valid values:

  • AWS: Production.

  • Sandbox: Testing environments.

Identifier.documentation: Specifies the ARN or the identifier of the bulk job.

ReportType.documentation: Specifies which records the report covers. If you omit this field, the report covers the records that failed.

GetCustomerAccountBulkJobReportUrlReques.documentation: Information about get customer account bulk job report url request.

ReportStatus.documentation: The status of the report. The Url is returned only when the status is AVAILABLE.

Url.documentation: A temporary URL for downloading the report. Present only when ReportStatus is AVAILABLE.

ExpiresAt.documentation: The date and time when the URL expires. Present only when ReportStatus is AVAILABLE.

FailureReason.documentation: The reason that the report couldn't be generated. Present only when ReportStatus is FAILED.

GetCustomerAccountBulkJobReportUrlRespon.documentation: Information about get customer account bulk job report url response.

Id.documentation: The unique identifier of the customer account.

EnrichmentStatus.documentation: The enrichment status of the customer account.

PartnerAccountIdentifier.documentation: Your own identifier for the customer account, if you provided one.

AwsEnrichment.documentation: Enrichment information that AWS provides about the customer. Present only when EnrichmentStatus is ENRICHED.

Account.documentation: The details of the customer that you provided.

Tags.documentation: The tags on the customer account. This member is absent if the tags can't be retrieved, which is different from an account that has no tags.

Filter.documentation: Specifies a filter tree that narrows the customer accounts. Each node either combines child filters or compares a single field to a value. If you omit this field, the statistics cover all of your customer accounts.

Aggregations.documentation: Specifies how to group the customer accounts. Each aggregation returns the number of accounts for each value of a field.

IncludeMissing.documentation: Specifies whether to include a group for customer accounts that have no value for the grouped field.

GetCustomerAccountStatisticsRequest.documentation: Information about get customer account statistics request.

TotalCount.documentation: The total number of customer accounts that match the filter.

Aggregations.documentation: The results of the aggregations, in the order that you requested them.

GetCustomerAccountStatisticsResponse.documentation: Information about get customer account statistics response.

Identifier.documentation: Specifies the unique identifier for the retrieved engagement invitation.

GetEngagementInvitationRequest.documentation: Contains the request parameters for the GetEngagementInvitation operation.

Arn.documentation: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that identifies the engagement invitation.

PayloadType.documentation: The type of payload contained in the engagement invitation, indicating what data or context the payload covers.

Id.documentation: Unique identifier assigned to the engagement invitation being retrieved.

EngagementId.documentation: The identifier of the engagement associated with this invitation.This ID links the invitation to its corresponding engagement.

EngagementTitle.documentation: The title of the engagement invitation, summarizing the purpose or objectives of the opportunity shared by AWS.

Status.documentation: The current status of the engagement invitation.

InvitationDate.documentation: The date when the engagement invitation was sent to the partner.

ExpirationDate.documentation: Indicates the date on which the engagement invitation will expire if not accepted by the partner.

SenderAwsAccountId.documentation: Specifies the AWS Account ID of the sender, which identifies the AWS team responsible for sharing the engagement invitation.

SenderCompanyName.documentation: The name of the AWS organization or team that sent the engagement invitation.

Receiver.documentation: Information about the partner organization or team that received the engagement invitation, including contact details and identifiers.

Catalog.documentation: Indicates the catalog from which the engagement invitation details are retrieved. This field helps in identifying the appropriate catalog (e.g., AWS or Sandbox) used in the request.

RejectionReason.documentation: If the engagement invitation was rejected, this field specifies the reason provided by the partner for the rejection.

Payload.documentation: Details of the engagement invitation payload, including specific data relevant to the invitation's contents, such as customer information and opportunity insights.

InvitationMessage.documentation: The message sent to the invited partner when the invitation was created.

EngagementDescription.documentation: The description of the engagement associated with this invitation.

ExistingMembers.documentation:
A list of active members currently part of the Engagement. This array contains a maximum of 10 members, each represented by an object with the following properties.

  • CompanyName: The name of the member's company.

  • WebsiteUrl: The website URL of the member's company.

EnrichmentContext.documentation: The enrichment data for the engagement associated with this invitation. You can view propensity scores, program eligibility, and lead readiness assessments before taking action on the invitation.

GetEngagementInvitationResponse.documentation: Contains the response that the GetEngagementInvitation action returns.

Catalog.documentation: Specifies the catalog related to the engagement request. Valid values are AWS and Sandbox.

Identifier.documentation: Specifies the identifier of the Engagement record to retrieve.

GetEngagementRequest.documentation: Contains the request parameters for the GetEngagement operation.

Id.documentation: The unique resource identifier of the engagement retrieved.

Arn.documentation: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the engagement retrieved.

Title.documentation: The title of the engagement. It provides a brief, descriptive name for the engagement that is meaningful and easily recognizable.

Description.documentation: A more detailed description of the engagement. This provides additional context or information about the engagement's purpose or scope.

CreatedAt.documentation: The date and time when the Engagement was created, presented in ISO 8601 format (UTC). For example: "2023-05-01T20:37:46Z". This timestamp helps track the lifecycle of the Engagement.

CreatedBy.documentation: The AWS account ID of the user who originally created the engagement. This field helps in tracking the origin of the engagement.

MemberCount.documentation: Specifies the current count of members participating in the Engagement. This count includes all active members regardless of their roles or permissions within the Engagement.

ModifiedAt.documentation: The timestamp indicating when the engagement was last modified, in ISO 8601 format (UTC). Example: "2023-05-01T20:37:46Z". This helps track the most recent changes to the engagement.

ModifiedBy.documentation: The AWS account ID of the user who last modified the engagement. This field helps track who made the most recent changes to the engagement.

Contexts.documentation: A list of context objects associated with the engagement. Each context provides additional information related to the Engagement, such as customer projects or documents.

GetEngagementResponse.documentation: Contains the response that the GetEngagement action returns.

GetOpportunityBulkJobReportUrlResponse.documentation: The status of the report and, when it is ready, the URL to download it.

PrimaryNeedsFromAws.documentation:
Identifies the type of support the partner needs from Amazon Web Services.

Valid values:

  • Cosell—Architectural Validation: Confirmation from Amazon Web Services that the partner's proposed solution architecture is aligned with Amazon Web Services best practices and poses minimal architectural risks.

  • Cosell—Business Presentation: Request Amazon Web Services seller's participation in a joint customer presentation.

  • Cosell—Competitive Information: Access to Amazon Web Services competitive resources and support for the partner's proposed solution.

  • Cosell—Pricing Assistance: Connect with an Amazon Web Services seller for support situations where a partner may be receiving an upfront discount on a service (for example: EDP deals).

  • Cosell—Technical Consultation: Connect with an Amazon Web Services Solutions Architect to address the partner's questions about the proposed solution.

  • Cosell—Total Cost of Ownership Evaluation: Assistance with quoting different cost savings of proposed solutions on Amazon Web Services versus on-premises or a traditional hosting environment.

  • Cosell—Deal Support: Request Amazon Web Services seller's support to progress the opportunity (for example: joint customer call, strategic positioning).

  • Cosell—Support for Public Tender/RFx: Opportunity related to the public sector where the partner needs Amazon Web Services RFx support.

NationalSecurity.documentation: Indicates whether the Opportunity pertains to a national security project. This field must be set to true only when the customer's industry is Government. Additional privacy and security measures apply during the review and management process for opportunities marked as NationalSecurity.

PartnerOpportunityIdentifier.documentation: Specifies the opportunity's unique identifier in the partner's CRM system. This value is essential to track and reconcile because it's included in the outbound payload sent back to the partner.

Customer.documentation: Specifies details of the customer associated with the Opportunity.

Project.documentation: An object that contains project details summary for the Opportunity.

OpportunityType.documentation:
Specifies the opportunity type as renewal, new, or expansion.

Opportunity types:

  • New opportunity: Represents a new business opportunity with a potential customer that's not previously engaged with your solutions or services.

  • Renewal opportunity: Represents an opportunity to renew an existing contract or subscription with a current customer, which helps to ensure service continuity.

  • Expansion opportunity: Represents an opportunity to expand the scope of a customer's contract or subscription, either by adding new services or increasing the volume of existing services.

Marketing.documentation: An object that contains marketing details for the Opportunity.

SoftwareRevenue.documentation: Specifies details of a customer's procurement terms. Required only for partners in eligible programs.

Id.documentation: Read-only, system generated Opportunity unique identifier.

Arn.documentation: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the opportunity.

LastModifiedDate.documentation: DateTime when the opportunity was last modified.

RelatedEntityIdentifiers.documentation: Provides information about the associations of other entities with the opportunity. These entities include identifiers for AWSProducts, Partner Solutions, and AWSMarketplaceOffers.

LifeCycle.documentation: An object that contains lifecycle details for the Opportunity.

OpportunityTeam.documentation: Represents the internal team handling the opportunity. Specify the members involved in collaborating on this opportunity within the partner's organization.

GetProspectingFromEngagementTaskRequest.documentation: Represents the request structure for retrieving the status and results of a prospecting task.

TaskName.documentation: The descriptive name of the task that you provided when you created it.

EndTime.documentation: The timestamp indicating when the task finished processing. This field is absent if the task is still in progress. The format follows ISO 8601 date-time notation.

Engagements.documentation: An array of EngagementProspectingResult entries for each engagement in the task. Each entry contains the processing status. For successfully completed engagements, includes the prospecting context identifier. For failed engagements, includes an error code and message.

ResourceSnapshotJobIdentifier.documentation: The unique identifier of the resource snapshot job to be retrieved. This identifier is crucial for pinpointing the specific job you want to query.

GetResourceSnapshotJobRequest.documentation: Contains the request parameters for the GetResourceSnapshotJob operation.

Catalog.documentation: The catalog in which the snapshot job was created. This will match the Catalog specified in the request.

Id.documentation: The unique identifier of the snapshot job. This matches the ResourceSnapshotJobIdentifier provided in the request.

Arn.documentation: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the snapshot job. This globally unique identifier can be used for resource-specific operations across AWS services.

EngagementId.documentation: The identifier of the engagement associated with this snapshot job. This links the job to a specific engagement context.

ResourceType.documentation: The type of resource being snapshotted. This would have "Opportunity" as a value as it is dependent on the supported resource type.

ResourceArn.documentation: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the resource being snapshotted. This provides a globally unique identifier for the resource across AWS.

BusinessProblem.documentation: Describes the business problem or challenge that the customer discussed during the interaction. This information helps qualify the lead and identify appropriate solutions.

LeadInteraction.documentation: Represents a specific interaction or touchpoint with a lead customer. This structure captures details about communications, meetings, or other engagement activities that help track the lead's progression and engagement history.

CountryCode.documentation: The country code indicating the geographic location of the customer company. This information helps partners understand regional requirements and assess their ability to serve the customer effectively.

AwsMaturity.documentation: Indicates the customer's level of experience and adoption with AWS services. This assessment helps partners understand the customer's cloud maturity and tailor their engagement approach accordingly.

MarketSegment.documentation: Specifies the market segment classification of the customer, such as enterprise, mid-market, or small business. This segmentation helps partners determine the appropriate solution complexity and engagement strategy.

Usecase.documentation: Describes the specific use case or business scenario associated with the lead interaction. This information helps partners understand the customer's interests and potential solution requirements.

LeadInvitationInteraction.documentation: Represents interaction details included in a lead invitation payload. This structure provides context about how the lead was generated and the customer's engagement history to help partners assess the opportunity quality.

Interaction.documentation: Describes the interaction details associated with the lead, including the source of the lead generation and customer engagement information. This context helps partners evaluate the lead quality and engagement approach.

LeadInvitationPayload.documentation: Represents the data payload of an engagement invitation for a lead opportunity. This contains detailed information about the customer and interaction history that partners use to evaluate whether to accept the lead engagement invitation.

LeadMarketSegment.documentation: The market segment that a lead's company belongs to.

Stage.documentation:
Specifies the current stage of the Opportunity's lifecycle as it maps to Amazon Web Services stages from the current stage in the partner CRM. This field provides a translated value of the stage, and offers insight into the Opportunity's progression in the sales cycle, according to Amazon Web Services definitions.

A lead and a prospect must be further matured to a Qualified opportunity before submission. Opportunities that were closed/lost before submission aren't suitable for submission.

The descriptions of each sales stage are:

  • Prospect: Amazon Web Services identifies the opportunity. It can be active (Comes directly from the end customer through a lead) or latent (Your account team believes it exists based on research, account plans, sales plays).

  • Qualified: Your account team engaged with the customer to discuss viability and requirements. The customer agreed that the opportunity is real, of interest, and may solve business/technical needs.

  • Technical Validation: All parties understand the implementation plan.

  • Business Validation: Pricing was proposed, and all parties agree to the steps to close.

  • Committed: The customer signed the contract, but Amazon Web Services hasn't started billing.

  • Launched: The workload is complete, and Amazon Web Services has started billing.

  • Closed Lost: The opportunity is lost, and there are no steps to move forward.

ClosedLostReason.documentation:
Specifies the reason code when an opportunity is marked as Closed Lost. When you select an appropriate reason code, you communicate the context for closing the Opportunity, and aid in accurate reports and analysis of opportunity outcomes. The possible values are:

  • Customer Deficiency: The customer lacked necessary resources or capabilities.

  • Delay/Cancellation of Project: The project was delayed or canceled.

  • Legal/Tax/Regulatory: Legal, tax, or regulatory issues prevented progress.

  • Lost to Competitor—Google: The opportunity was lost to Google.

  • Lost to Competitor—Microsoft: The opportunity was lost to Microsoft.

  • Lost to Competitor—SoftLayer: The opportunity was lost to SoftLayer.

  • Lost to Competitor—VMWare: The opportunity was lost to VMWare.

  • Lost to Competitor—Other: The opportunity was lost to a competitor not listed above.

  • No Opportunity: There was no opportunity to pursue.

  • On Premises Deployment: The customer chose an on-premises solution.

  • Partner Gap: The partner lacked necessary resources or capabilities.

  • Price: The price was not competitive or acceptable to the customer.

  • Security/Compliance: Security or compliance issues prevented progress.

  • Technical Limitations: Technical limitations prevented progress.

  • Customer Experience: Issues related to the customer's experience impacted the decision.

Specifies the current stage of the Opportunity's lifecycle as it maps to Amazon Web Services stages from the current stage in the partner CRM. A lead and a prospect must be further matured to a Qualified opportunity before submission. Opportunities that were closed/lost before submission aren't suitable for submission.

The descriptions of each sales stage are:

  • Prospect: Amazon Web Services identifies the opportunity. It can be active (Comes directly from the end customer through a lead) or latent (Your account team believes it exists based on research, account plans, sales plays).

  • Qualified: Your account team engaged with the customer to discuss viability and understand requirements. The customer agreed that the opportunity is real, of interest, and may solve business/technical needs.

  • Technical Validation: All parties understand the implementation plan.

  • Business Validation: Pricing was proposed, and all parties agree to the steps to close.

  • Committed: The customer signed the contract, but Amazon Web Services hasn't started billing.

  • Launched: The workload is complete, and Amazon Web Services has started billing.

  • Closed Lost: The opportunity is lost, and there are no steps to move forward.
