This field captures the identifier used to track and categorize the Opportunity within marketing campaigns. If you don't have a campaign code, contact your Amazon Web Services point of contact to obtain one.

Source.documentation: Indicates if the Opportunity was sourced from an Amazon Web Services marketing activity. Use the value Marketing Activity. Use None if it's not associated with an Amazon Web Services marketing activity. This field helps Amazon Web Services track the return on marketing investments and enables better distribution of marketing budgets among partners.

UseCases.documentation:
Specifies the marketing activity use case or purpose that led to the Opportunity's creation or contact. This field captures the context or marketing activity's execution's intention and the direct correlation to the generated opportunity or contact. Must be empty when Marketing.AWSFundingUsed = No.

Valid values: AI/ML | Analytics | Application Integration | Blockchain | Business Applications | Cloud Financial Management | Compute | Containers | Customer Engagement | Databases | Developer Tools | End User Computing | Front End Web & Mobile | Game Tech | IoT | Management & Governance | Media Services | Migration & Transfer | Networking & Content Delivery | Quantum Technologies | Robotics | Satellite | Security | Serverless | Storage | VR & AR

Channels.documentation: Specifies the Opportunity's channel that the marketing activity is associated with or was contacted through. This field provides information about the specific marketing channel that contributed to the generation of the lead or contact.

AwsFundingUsed.documentation: Indicates if the Opportunity is a marketing development fund (MDF) funded activity.

Marketing.documentation: An object that contains marketing details for the Opportunity.

MarketingSource.documentation: The source of the marketing activity. Valid values are Marketing Activity and None.

MaxResults.documentation: Information about max results.

MemberCompanyName.documentation: The name of the company that an engagement member belongs to.

MemberPageSize.documentation: The maximum number of engagement members that a single call returns. The default is 5. Valid values range from 1 to 10.

MonetaryAmount.documentation: A monetary amount written as a decimal number with up to two digits after the decimal point.

CurrencyCode.documentation: Specifies the payment currency. Accepted values are USD (US Dollars) and EUR (Euros). If the AWS Partition is aws-eusc (AWS European Sovereign Cloud), the currency code must be EUR.

Name.documentation: The name of a person or a company.

NationalSecurity.documentation: Specifies whether the opportunity involves national security. The value is Yes if it does, or No if it doesn't.

NextStepsHistory.documentation: Read-only; shows the last 50 values and change dates for the NextSteps field.

NextToken.documentation: Information about next token.

OpportunityArn.documentation: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that identifies an opportunity.

JobId.documentation: The unique identifier of the bulk job.

Status.documentation: The current status of the bulk job.

TotalRecords.documentation: The total number of records in the input file.

ProcessedRecords.documentation: The number of records that Partner Central has processed so far.

CreatedAt.documentation: The date and time, in UTC, when you created the bulk job.

StartedAt.documentation: The date and time, in UTC, when the bulk job started processing records.

CompletedAt.documentation: The date and time, in UTC, when the bulk job finished.

FailureReason.documentation: The reason that the bulk job failed. Present only when Status is FAILED.

FileName.documentation: The name of the input file that started the bulk job. Use it to identify the job by its file.

OperationType.documentation: Indicates whether the bulk job creates or updates opportunities, based on the template of the input file. Partner Central doesn't set this field until it reads the file.

OpportunityBulkJobSummary.documentation: The status, record counts, and input file name of an opportunity bulk job.

OpportunityBulkJobSummaryList.documentation: The list of opportunity bulk job summaries.

SortOrder.documentation: Defines the order in which the Engagement Invitations are sorted. The values can be ASC (ascending) or DESC (descending).

SortBy.documentation: Specifies the field by which the Engagement Invitations are sorted. Common values include InvitationDate and Status.

OpportunityEngagementInvitationSort.documentation: Defines sorting options for retrieving Engagement Invitations. Sorting can be done based on various criteria like the invitation date or status.

OpportunityEngagementInvitationSortName.documentation: The name of the field that sorts a list of engagement invitations. The only valid value is InvitationDate.

OpportunityIdentifier.documentation: The identifier of an opportunity. An identifier starts with the letter O followed by up to 19 digits.

SenderContacts.documentation: Represents the contact details of the AWS representatives involved in sending the Engagement Invitation. These contacts are opportunity stakeholders.

ReceiverResponsibilities.documentation: Outlines the responsibilities or expectations of the receiver in the context of the invitation.

Customer.documentation: Contains information about the customer related to the opportunity in the Engagement Invitation. This data helps partners understand the customer’s profile and requirements.

Project.documentation: Describes the project details associated with the opportunity, including the customer’s needs and the scope of work expected to be performed.

OpportunityType.documentation:
The type of the opportunity being shared. The sender of the invitation sets it. Valid values:

  • Net New Business: A new business opportunity with a potential customer that's not previously engaged with your solutions or services.

  • Flat Renewal: An opportunity to renew an existing contract or subscription with a current customer, ensuring continuity of service.

  • Expansion: An opportunity to expand the scope of an existing contract or subscription, either by adding new services or increasing the volume of existing services for a current customer.

OpportunityInvitationPayload.documentation: Represents the data payload of an Engagement Invitation for a specific opportunity. This contains detailed information that partners use to evaluate the engagement.

OpportunityOrigin.documentation: The origin of an opportunity. Valid values are AWS Referral and Partner Referral.

Score.documentation: Deal quality score assigned to the opportunity. Values range from 0 to 100.

Trend.documentation: Direction of score change since last scoring iteration. Known values: Improving, Declining, No Change.

CompanyName.documentation: The name of the end customer company on the opportunity.

Industry.documentation: The industry of the end customer on the opportunity.

AwsAccountId.documentation: The end customer company's AWS account ID, if known or available.

Address.documentation: The end customer address details for the opportunity.

OpportunitySearchAccount.documentation: Contains the end customer account fields (company name, industry, AWS account ID, and address) returned for an opportunity in search results.

CountryCode.documentation: The country of the end customer, in ISO 3166 alpha-2 format.

OpportunitySearchAddress.documentation: Contains the end customer address fields (country) returned for an opportunity in search results.

Origin.documentation: Specifies whether the opportunity originated from AWS or from the partner.

CosellMotion.documentation: The engagement classification for this opportunity. Read-only.

Insights.documentation: Curated insights returned in search results: the engagement score and quality score.

OpportunitySearchAwsSummary.documentation: Contains the AWS-sourced fields (co-sell motion and a trimmed set of insights) returned for an opportunity in search results.

Account.documentation: The end customer account details for the opportunity.

OpportunitySearchCustomer.documentation: Contains the end customer fields (company name, industry, AWS account, and country) returned for an opportunity in search results.

CurrencyCode.documentation: The currency of the estimated amount, in ISO 4217 format.

OpportunitySearchExpectedCustomerSpend.documentation: A curated expected-spend entry: amount and currency only. Frequency and target company are omitted from search results.

OpportunitySearchExpectedCustomerSpendLi.documentation: A list of the amounts that you expect the customer to spend, as shown in search results.

AndAllFilters.documentation: A list of sub-filters that are joined with a logical AND. The node matches only when every sub-filter matches.

OrAllFilters.documentation: A list of sub-filters that are joined with a logical OR. The node matches when at least one sub-filter matches.

NotFilter.documentation: A single sub-filter that is negated. The node matches when the sub-filter does not match.

EqualsTo.documentation: A leaf condition that matches when the field equals the supplied value.

ContainsAny.documentation: A leaf condition that matches when the field contains any of the supplied values as a case-insensitive substring. On a multi-valued field, the condition matches when any element contains the substring.

ContainsAll.documentation: A leaf condition that matches when the field holds every supplied value. On a multi-valued field, every listed value must be present.

GreaterThan.documentation: A leaf condition that matches when the field is greater than the supplied value. Supported on ordered fields only (date or numeric).

GreaterThanOrEquals.documentation: A leaf condition that matches when the field is greater than or equal to the supplied value. Supported on ordered fields only (date or numeric).

LessThan.documentation: A leaf condition that matches when the field is less than the supplied value. Supported on ordered fields only (date or numeric).

LessThanOrEquals.documentation: A leaf condition that matches when the field is less than or equal to the supplied value. Supported on ordered fields only (date or numeric).

OpportunitySearchFilter.documentation: A recursive filter node. Exactly one member must be set. The boolean combinators nest sub-filters: AndAllFilters joins its children with AND, OrAllFilters matches when at least one child matches, and NotFilter negates its single child. The remaining members are leaf conditions over a single field. Nesting is bounded (depth up to 3, each combinator list up to 10 entries, and up to 20 leaf conditions per tree). If a request exceeds these limits, the service returns a ValidationException.

OpportunitySearchFilterList.documentation: A list of sub-filters in an opportunity search filter.

OpportunitySearchFilterName.documentation: The name of an opportunity field that an opportunity search condition can apply to.

StringValue.documentation: A single string value. Used by EqualsTo, and by ContainsAny or ContainsAll for a single-value match.

StringListValue.documentation: A list of string values. Used by ContainsAny or ContainsAll to match against multiple values.

LongValue.documentation: An integral numeric value, used by the range comparisons on integral numeric fields.

DoubleValue.documentation: A fractional numeric value, used by the range comparisons on numeric amount fields such as EstimatedMrr.

DateValue.documentation: A date-time value in RFC 3339 format, used by the range comparisons on date fields.

OpportunitySearchFilterValue.documentation: Contains the value that a search predicate compares against. Specify exactly one member. The member you choose must match the field type and the comparison operator of the predicate.

OpportunitySearchFilterValues.documentation: A list of string values that an opportunity search condition compares against.

EngagementScore.documentation: The level of engagement with the opportunity. The value is High, Medium, or Low.

OpportunityQuality.documentation: The opportunity quality score. Null when the opportunity has not yet been scored.

OpportunitySearchInsights.documentation: Contains the insight scores (engagement score and opportunity quality score) returned for an opportunity in search results.

NextSteps.documentation: The next steps for the opportunity. Mandatory for co-sell opportunities.

TargetCloseDate.documentation: The projected launch date of the opportunity, in ISO 8601 (YYYY-MM-DD) format.

OpportunitySearchLifeCycle.documentation: Contains the lifecycle fields (review status, stage, next steps, and target close date) returned for an opportunity in search results.

Score.documentation: A deal quality score (0-100) assigned to the opportunity.

Key.documentation: The opportunity field that the condition applies to.

Value.documentation:
The typed value the condition compares against. Specify one of the following:

  • A single string value – used by EqualsTo, and by ContainsAny or ContainsAll for a single-value match.

  • A list of string values – used by ContainsAny or ContainsAll to match against multiple values.

  • An integral numeric value – used by the range comparisons on integral numeric fields.

  • A fractional numeric value – used by the range comparisons on numeric amount fields such as EstimatedMrr.

  • A date-time value in RFC 3339 format – used by the range comparisons on date fields.

OpportunitySearchPredicate.documentation: A leaf filter condition. It carries the field (Key) and the typed value (Value) to compare against. The enclosing OpportunitySearchFilter member determines the comparison operator.

ApnPrograms.documentation: The AWS Partner Network (APN) programs associated with the opportunity's products or services.

ExpectedCustomerSpend.documentation: The estimated AWS monthly recurring revenue (MRR): amount and currency only.

OpportunitySearchProject.documentation: Contains the project fields (title, AWS Partner Network (APN) programs, and expected customer spend) returned for an opportunity in search results.

AwsMarketplaceOffers.documentation: The AWS Marketplace offers associated with this opportunity.

AwsMarketplaceOfferSets.documentation: The AWS Marketplace offer sets associated with this opportunity.

AwsMarketplaceSolutions.documentation: The AWS Marketplace solutions associated with this opportunity.

Solutions.documentation: The proposed solutions to address the customer's business problem.

OpportunitySearchRelatedEntityIdentifier.documentation: Contains the related-entity identifiers (AWS Marketplace offers, offer sets, and solutions) returned for an opportunity in search results.

SortBy.documentation: The field to sort the results by.

SortOrder.documentation: The direction of the sort, either ascending or descending.

OpportunitySearchSortName.documentation: The name of an opportunity field that you can use to sort opportunity search results.

OpportunitySearchSummaries.documentation: A list of opportunity summaries that an opportunity search returns.

Id.documentation: The read-only, system-generated unique identifier of the opportunity.

LastModifiedDate.documentation: The date and time when the opportunity was last modified, in UTC.

CreatedDate.documentation: The date and time when the opportunity was created, in UTC.

OpportunityType.documentation: Specifies whether the opportunity is a new business opportunity, a renewal, or an expansion.

PartnerOpportunityIdentifier.documentation: The unique identifier of the opportunity in your customer relationship management (CRM) system. This value lets you link the opportunity to your CRM.

LifeCycle.documentation: A curated lifecycle view: review status, stage, next steps, and target close date.

Customer.documentation: A curated customer view: company name, industry, AWS account, and country.

Project.documentation: A curated project view: title, AWS Partner Network (APN) programs, and expected customer spend.

Tags.documentation: The tags associated with the opportunity, returned as key-value pairs.

RelatedEntityIdentifiers.documentation: Curated related-entity identifiers surfaced in search: AWS Marketplace offers, offer sets, and solutions.

OpportunityTeam.documentation: The opportunity owner and team members. Search results include only each member's name and business title, and exclude contact email and phone.

AwsOpportunitySummary.documentation: The AWS-side view of this opportunity. Absent when no AWS opportunity summary record exists yet.

OpportunitySearchSummary.documentation: A curated summary view of an opportunity returned by a search. It holds the fields needed to render a search result row, take action, and run follow-up filters.

OpportunitySearchTeamMember.documentation: An opportunity team member surfaced in search: name and business title only, with no contact details.

OpportunitySearchTeamMembersList.documentation: A list of the opportunity team members that search results show.

OpportunitySortName.documentation: The name of the field that sorts a list of opportunities.

Catalog.documentation: Specifies the catalog associated with the opportunity, either AWS or Sandbox. This indicates the environment in which the opportunity is managed.

Id.documentation: Read-only, system-generated Opportunity unique identifier.

Arn.documentation: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) for the opportunity. This globally unique identifier can be used for IAM policies and cross-service references.

PartnerOpportunityIdentifier.documentation: Specifies the Opportunity's unique identifier in the partner's CRM system. This value is essential to track and reconcile because it's included in the outbound payload sent back to the partner. It allows partners to link an opportunity to their CRM.

OpportunityType.documentation:
Specifies opportunity type as a renewal, new, or expansion.

Opportunity types:

  • New Opportunity: Represents a new business opportunity with a potential customer that's not previously engaged with your solutions or services.

  • Renewal Opportunity: Represents an opportunity to renew an existing contract or subscription with a current customer, ensuring continuity of service.

  • Expansion Opportunity: Represents an opportunity to expand the scope of an existing contract or subscription, either by adding new services or increasing the volume of existing services for a current customer.

LifeCycle.documentation: An object that contains the Opportunity's lifecycle details.

Customer.documentation: An object that contains the Opportunity's customer details.

Project.documentation: An object that contains the Opportunity's project details summary.

OpportunitySummary.documentation: An object that contains an Opportunity's subset of fields.

Lifecycle.documentation: Contains information about the opportunity's lifecycle, including its current stage, status, and important dates such as creation and last modification times.

OpportunityTeam.documentation: Represents the internal team handling the opportunity. Specify the members involved in collaborating on an opportunity within the partner's organization.

PrimaryNeedsFromAws.documentation: Identifies the type of support the partner needs from AWS.

Customer.documentation: Contains details about the customer that the opportunity belongs to.

Project.documentation: Contains summary information about the project associated with the opportunity, including project name, description, timeline, and other relevant details.

RelatedEntityIdentifiers.documentation: Lists the identifiers of entities that relate to the opportunity, such as AWS products, partner solutions, and AWS Marketplace offers.

OpportunitySummaryView.documentation: Provides a comprehensive view of an opportunity summary, including lifecycle information, team details, opportunity type, primary needs from AWS, and associated project information.

OpportunityType.documentation: The type of an opportunity. Valid values are Net New Business, Flat Renewal, and Expansion.

PageSize.documentation: The maximum number of results that a single call returns. Valid values range from 1 to 100. If you don't specify a value, the operation uses its default page size.

ParticipantType.documentation: The role of the caller in an engagement invitation. Valid values are SENDER and RECEIVER.

PartnerOpportunityTeamMembersList.documentation: A list of the partner's team members who work on the opportunity.

OpportunityInvitation.documentation: Specifies the details of the opportunity invitation within the Engagement Invitation payload. This data helps partners understand the context, scope, and expected involvement for the opportunity from AWS.

LeadInvitation.documentation: Specifies the details of the lead invitation within the Engagement Invitation payload. This data helps partners understand the lead context, customer information, and interaction history for the lead opportunity from AWS.

AccountPlanningInvitation.documentation: The content of an account-planning invitation. This field is present when the invitation is for account planning.

Payload.documentation: Contains the data payload associated with the Engagement Invitation. This payload includes essential details related to the AWS opportunity and is used by partners to evaluate whether to accept or reject the engagement.

PaymentFrequency.documentation: How often the customer pays the expected spend. Set this value to Monthly.

PhoneNumber.documentation: A phone number in international format, which starts with a plus sign followed by the country code and the number.

Timezone.documentation: The IANA time zone name that the window is expressed in, for example America/Chicago.

PreferredContactWindow.documentation: The time window during which the sender prefers to be contacted about an account plan. This information is advisory. Both fields are optional.

PrimaryNeedFromAws.documentation: A type of help that the partner needs from AWS on an opportunity.
enum: Co-Sell - Total Cost of Ownership Evaluation
Co-Sell - Support for Public Tender / RFx

PrimaryNeedsFromAws.documentation: A list of the types of help that the partner needs from AWS on an opportunity.

Value.documentation: Represents the details of the next step recorded, such as follow-up actions or decisions made. This field helps in tracking progress and ensuring alignment with project goals.

Time.documentation: Indicates the date and time when a particular next step was recorded or planned. This helps in managing the timeline for the opportunity.

ProfileNextStepsHistory.documentation: Tracks the history of next steps associated with the opportunity. This field captures the actions planned for the future and their timeline.

DeliveryModels.documentation:
Specifies the deployment or consumption model for your solution or service in the Opportunity's context. You can select multiple options.

Options' descriptions from the Delivery Model field are:

  • SaaS or PaaS: Your Amazon Web Services based solution deployed as SaaS or PaaS in your Amazon Web Services environment.

  • BYOL or AMI: Your Amazon Web Services based solution deployed as BYOL or AMI in the end customer's Amazon Web Services environment.

  • Managed Services: The end customer's Amazon Web Services business management (For example: Consulting, design, implementation, billing support, cost optimization, technical support).

  • Professional Services: Offerings to help enterprise end customers achieve specific business outcomes for enterprise cloud adoption (For example: Advisory or transformation planning).

  • Resell: Amazon Web Services accounts and billing management for your customers.

  • Other: Delivery model not described above.

ExpectedCustomerSpend.documentation: Represents the estimated amount that the customer is expected to spend on AWS services related to the opportunity. This helps in evaluating the potential financial value of the opportunity for AWS.

ExpectedContractDuration.documentation: Optional. The expected duration of the contract associated with this opportunity. Partners use this value alongside expected customer spend to convert Total Contract Value (TCV) into Monthly Recurring Revenue (MRR).

ApnPrograms.documentation:
Specifies the Amazon Partner Network (APN) program that influenced the Opportunity. APN programs refer to specific partner programs or initiatives that can impact the Opportunity.

Valid values: APN Immersion Days | APN Solution Space | ATO (Authority to Operate) | AWS Marketplace Campaign | IS Immersion Day SFID Program | ISV Workload Migration | Migration Acceleration Program | P3 | Partner Launch Initiative | Partner Opportunity Acceleration Funded | The Next Smart | VMware Cloud on AWS | Well-Architected | Windows | Workspaces/AppStream Accelerator Program | WWPS NDPP

CustomerBusinessProblem.documentation: Describes the problem the end customer has, and how the partner is helping. Utilize this field to provide a concise narrative that outlines the customer's business challenge or issue. Elaborate on how the partner's solution or offerings align to resolve the customer's business problem. Include relevant information about the partner's value proposition, unique selling points, and expertise to tackle the issue. Offer insights on how the proposed solution meets the customer's needs and provides value. Use concise language and precise descriptions to convey the context and significance of the Opportunity. The content in this field helps Amazon Web Services understand the nature of the Opportunity and the strategic fit of the partner's solution.

CustomerUseCase.documentation:
Specifies the proposed solution focus or type of workload for the Opportunity. This field captures the primary use case or objective of the proposed solution, and provides context and clarity to the addressed workload.

Valid values: AI Machine Learning and Analytics | Archiving | Big Data: Data Warehouse/Data Integration/ETL/Data Lake/BI | Blockchain | Business Applications: Mainframe Modernization | Business Applications & Contact Center | Business Applications & SAP Production | Centralized Operations Management | Cloud Management Tools | Cloud Management Tools & DevOps with Continuous Integration & Continuous Delivery (CICD) | Configuration, Compliance & Auditing | Connected Services | Containers & Serverless | Content Delivery & Edge Services | Database | Edge Computing/End User Computing | Energy | Enterprise Governance & Controls | Enterprise Resource Planning | Financial Services | Healthcare and Life Sciences | High Performance Computing | Hybrid Application Platform | Industrial Software | IOT | Manufacturing, Supply Chain and Operations | Media & High performance computing (HPC) | Migration/Database Migration | Monitoring, logging and performance | Monitoring & Observability | Networking | Outpost | SAP | Security & Compliance | Storage & Backup | Training | VMC | VMWare | Web development & DevOps

RelatedOpportunityIdentifier.documentation: Specifies the current opportunity's parent opportunity identifier.

SalesActivities.documentation:
Specifies the Opportunity's sales activities conducted with the end customer. These activities help drive Amazon Web Services assignment priority.

Valid values:

  • Initialized discussions with customer: Initial conversations with the customer to understand their needs and introduce your solution.

  • Customer has shown interest in solution: After initial discussions, the customer is interested in your solution.

  • Conducted POC/demo: You conducted a proof of concept (POC) or demonstration of the solution for the customer.

  • In evaluation/planning stage: The customer is evaluating the solution and planning potential implementation.

  • Agreed on solution to Business Problem: Both parties agree on how the solution addresses the customer's business problem.

  • Completed Action Plan: A detailed action plan is complete and outlines the steps for implementation.

  • Finalized Deployment Need: Both parties agree with and finalized the deployment needs.

  • SOW Signed: Both parties signed a statement of work (SOW), and formalize the agreement and detail the project scope and deliverables.

CompetitorName.documentation: Name of the Opportunity's competitor (if any). Use Other to submit a value not in the picklist.

OtherSolutionDescription.documentation: Specifies the offered solution for the customer's business problem when the RelatedEntityIdentifiers.Solutions field value is Other.

AdditionalComments.documentation: Captures additional comments or information for the Opportunity that weren't captured in other fields.

AwsPartition.documentation: AWS partition where the opportunity will be deployed. Possible values: aws-eusc for AWS European Sovereign Cloud, null for all other partitions.

Project.documentation: An object that contains the Opportunity's project details.

Title.documentation: Specifies the title of the project. This title helps partners quickly identify and understand the focus of the project.

TargetCompletionDate.documentation: Specifies the estimated date of project completion. This field helps track the project timeline and manage expectations.

ExpectedCustomerSpend.documentation: Contains revenue estimates for the partner related to the project. This field provides an idea of the financial potential of the opportunity for the partner.

ProjectDetails.documentation: Contains details about the project associated with the Engagement Invitation, including the business problem and expected outcomes.

ExpectedContractDuration.documentation: Optional. The expected contract duration for this opportunity, representing the anticipated length of the contract in the unit specified by Term.

SortBy.documentation: The field by which to sort the returned tasks. Valid values: StartTime (task creation timestamp), TaskName (alphabetically by task name), and FailedEngagementCount (number of failed engagements).

ProspectingFromEngagementTaskSort.documentation: Specifies the sort configuration for ListProspectingFromEngagementTasks. Contains the field to sort by and the sort direction.

ProspectingFromEngagementTaskSortName.documentation: The fields available for sorting results from ListProspectingFromEngagementTasks. Valid values are StartTime, TaskName, and FailedEngagementCount.

ProspectingGeo.documentation: The geographic area of the prospected customer.

MarketplaceEngagementScore.documentation: A score that indicates the prospected customer's level of engagement with AWS Marketplace. Valid values are High, Medium, and Low.

SolutionScore.documentation: A score that indicates how well the partner's solution fits the prospected customer's needs.

SolutionCategory.documentation: The primary solution category classification for the prospected customer. This indicates the type of solution that best addresses their needs.

SolutionSubCategory.documentation: The solution sub-category classification for the prospected customer. This provides more granular categorization of the recommended solution type.

ProspectingInsights.documentation: Contains insights that AI generates from the prospecting analysis. These insights include marketplace engagement scoring, solution fit assessments, and solution categorization for the prospected customer.

ProspectingPublicProfileSummary.documentation: A summary of the public profile of the prospected customer.

Aws.documentation: Prospecting data and insights that AWS provides during the prospecting job. This includes customer details, task information, and scoring that AI generates.

ProspectingResult.documentation: Contains the results of an autonomous prospecting job. This includes data and insights that AWS provides about a prospected customer account.

Customer.documentation: Contains details about the prospected customer account, including geographic, industry, and segment classifications.

Insights.documentation: Insights that AI generates from the prospecting analysis. These insights include engagement scores and solution fit assessments for the prospected customer.

StartTime.documentation: The timestamp when the prospecting result context was created. The format is ISO 8601 (UTC).

EndTime.documentation: The timestamp when the prospecting task completed processing. The format is ISO 8601 (UTC).

TaskId.documentation: The unique identifier of the prospecting task that generates this result.

TaskArn.documentation: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the prospecting task. Use this ARN to track and manage the task within AWS.

TaskName.documentation: The name that the user provides for the prospecting task that generates this result.

ProspectingResultAws.documentation: Contains the prospecting data that AWS sources. This includes task execution details, customer account information, and insights that AI generates from the prospecting analysis.

AccountName.documentation: The name of the prospected customer account.

Geo.documentation: The geographic region classification of the prospected customer account.

Region.documentation: The specific region of the prospected customer account.

SubRegion.documentation: The subregion classification of the prospected customer account.

Country.documentation: The country code of the prospected customer account.

Industry.documentation: The industry classification of the prospected customer account.

SubIndustry.documentation: The sub-industry classification of the prospected customer account. This provides more granular categorization within the primary industry.

Segment.documentation: The market segment classification of the prospected customer account.

CompanySize.documentation: The company size classification of the prospected customer account.

EligiblePrograms.documentation: A list of AWS Greenfield programs that the prospected customer is eligible for. Use this list to identify relevant go-to-market opportunities.

PublicProfileSummary.documentation: A summary of publicly available information about the prospected customer. The system uses this summary to generate customer insights and inform engagement strategies.

ProspectingResultCustomer.documentation: Contains detailed information about the prospected customer account, including company identifiers, geographic classification, industry segmentation, and program eligibility.

ProspectingSegment.documentation: The market segment of the prospected customer.

ProspectingTaskArn.documentation: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that identifies a prospecting task.

ProspectingTaskIdentifier.documentation: The identifier of a prospecting task. An identifier starts with task- followed by 14 lowercase letters or digits.

ProspectingTaskStatus.documentation: The current execution state of a prospecting task. A task transitions from PENDING to IN_PROGRESS when processing begins, and then to either COMPLETED or FAILED when processing ends.

TaskId.documentation: The unique identifier of the task. Use this value with GetProspectingFromEngagementTask to retrieve full task details.

TaskArn.documentation: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the task.

TaskName.documentation: The descriptive name of the task provided when it was created.

StartTime.documentation: The timestamp indicating when the task was initiated. The format follows ISO 8601 date-time notation.

EndTime.documentation: The timestamp indicating when the task finished processing. This field is absent if the task is still in progress. The format follows ISO 8601 date-time notation.

TotalEngagementCount.documentation: The total number of engagements included in the task.

CompletedEngagementCount.documentation: The number of engagements that have been successfully converted into prospecting leads.

FailedEngagementCount.documentation: The number of engagements that failed to be converted. Retrieve the full task details using GetProspectingFromEngagementTask for per-engagement error information.

ProspectingTaskSummary.documentation: A summary of a single prospecting task, returned by ListProspectingFromEngagementTasks. Contains key metrics and status information without the full per-engagement detail available from GetProspectingFromEngagementTask.

ProspectingTaskSummaryList.documentation: A list of summaries of prospecting tasks.

Catalog.documentation: Specifies the catalog in which the settings will be updated. Acceptable values include AWS for production and Sandbox for testing environments.

ResourceSnapshotJobRoleIdentifier.documentation: Specifies the ARN of the IAM Role used for resource snapshot job executions.

PutSellingSystemSettingsRequest.documentation: Contains the request parameters for the PutSellingSystemSettings operation.

Catalog.documentation: Specifies the catalog in which the settings are defined. Acceptable values include AWS for production and Sandbox for testing environments.

ResourceSnapshotJobRoleArn.documentation: Specifies the ARN of the IAM Role used for resource snapshot job executions.

PutSellingSystemSettingsResponse.documentation: Contains the response that the PutSellingSystemSettings action returns.

ReadinessLevel.documentation: The readiness level of an engagement group, which indicates the recommended call to action for its leads.

ReasonCode.documentation: A code that identifies the reason that a task failed.

Account.documentation: Specifies the AWS account of the partner who received the Engagement Invitation. This field is used to track the invitation recipient within the AWS ecosystem.

Receiver.documentation: Represents the entity that received the Engagement Invitation, including account and company details. This field is essential for tracking the partner who is being invited to collaborate.

ReceiverResponsibility.documentation: A responsibility that the receiver of an engagement invitation has in the engagement.

ReceiverResponsibilityList.documentation: A list of responsibilities that the receiver of an engagement invitation has in the engagement.

RecommendationAttributeMap.documentation: A map of key-value pairs that hold extra details about a recommendation. The map can contain up to 25 entries.

Catalog.documentation: This is the catalog that's associated with the engagement invitation. Acceptable values are AWS or Sandbox, and these values determine the environment in which the opportunity is managed.

Identifier.documentation: This is the unique identifier of the rejected EngagementInvitation. Providing the correct identifier helps to ensure that the intended invitation is rejected.

RejectionReason.documentation:
This describes the reason for rejecting the engagement invitation, which helps AWS track usage patterns. Acceptable values include the following:

  • Customer problem unclear: The customer's problem isn't understood.

  • Next steps unclear: The next steps required to proceed aren't understood.

  • Unable to support: The partner is unable to provide support due to resource or capability constraints.

  • Duplicate of partner referral: The opportunity is a duplicate of an existing referral.

  • Other: Any reason not covered by other values.

RejectEngagementInvitationRequest.documentation: Contains the request parameters for the RejectEngagementInvitation operation.

RejectionReasonString.documentation: The reason for rejecting an engagement invitation.

AwsMarketplaceOffers.documentation:
Takes one value per opportunity. Each value is an Amazon Resource Name (ARN), in this format: "offers": ["arn:aws:aws-marketplace:us-east-1:999999999999:AWSMarketplace/Offer/offer-sampleOffer32"].

Use the ListEntities action in the Marketplace Catalog APIs for a list of offers in the associated Marketplace seller account.

AwsMarketplaceOfferSets.documentation: Enables the association of AWS Marketplace offer sets with the Opportunity. Offer sets allow grouping multiple related marketplace offers together for comprehensive solution packaging. Each value is an Amazon Resource Name (ARN) in this format: arn:aws:aws-marketplace:us-east-1:999999999999:AWSMarketplace/OfferSet/offerset-sampleOfferSet32.

Solutions.documentation:
Enables partner solutions or offerings' association with an opportunity. To associate a solution, provide the solution's unique identifier, which you can obtain with the ListSolutions operation.

If the specific solution identifier is not available, you can use the value Other and provide details about the solution in the otherSolutionOffered field. But when the opportunity reaches the Committed stage or beyond, the Other value cannot be used, and a valid solution identifier must be provided.

By associating the relevant solutions with the opportunity, you can communicate the offerings that are being considered or implemented to address the customer's business problem.

AwsProducts.documentation:
Enables the association of specific Amazon Web Services products with the Opportunity. Partners can indicate the relevant Amazon Web Services products for the Opportunity's solution and align with the customer's needs. Returns multiple values separated by commas. For example, "AWSProducts" : ["AmazonRedshift", "AWSAppFabric", "AWSCleanRooms"].

Use the file with the list of Amazon Web Services products hosted on GitHub: Amazon Web Services products.

AwsMarketplaceSolutions.documentation: Specifies the AWS Marketplace solutions to associate with the Opportunity. Each value is an Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that identifies a solution listing in AWS Marketplace.

AwsMarketplaceProducts.documentation: Specifies the AWS Marketplace products to associate with the Opportunity. Each value is an Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that identifies a product listing in AWS Marketplace.

RelatedEntityIdentifiers.documentation: This field provides the associations' information for other entities with the opportunity. These entities include identifiers for AWSProducts, Partner Solutions, and AWSMarketplaceOffers.

RelatedEntityType.documentation: The type of an entity that you associate with an opportunity. Valid values are Solutions, AwsProducts, AwsMarketplaceOffers, AwsMarketplaceOfferSets, AwsMarketplaceSolutions, and AwsMarketplaceProducts.

ResourceArn.documentation: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that identifies a resource.

ResourceIdentifier.documentation: The identifier of a resource. For the Opportunity resource type, the identifier is an opportunity identifier.

Message.documentation: A message that describes which resource the service couldn't find.

ResourceNotFoundException.documentation:
This error occurs when the specified resource can't be found. The resource might not exist, or isn't visible with the current credentials.

Suggested action: Verify that the resource ID is correct and the resource is in the expected AWS region. Check IAM permissions for accessing the resource.

ResourceSnapshotArn.documentation: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that identifies a resource snapshot.

ResourceSnapshotJobArn.documentation: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that identifies a resource snapshot job.

ResourceSnapshotJobIdentifier.documentation: The identifier of a resource snapshot job. An identifier starts with job- followed by 13 lowercase letters or digits.

ResourceSnapshotJobRoleArn.documentation: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) role that a resource snapshot job uses.

ResourceSnapshotJobRoleIdentifier.documentation: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) or the name of the AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) role that a resource snapshot job uses.

ResourceSnapshotJobStatus.documentation: The status of a resource snapshot job. Running means the job is actively running. Stopped means the job isn't running.

Id.documentation: The unique identifier for the resource snapshot job within the AWS Partner Central system. This ID is used for direct references to the job within the service.

Arn.documentation: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) for the resource snapshot job.

Status.documentation:
The current status of the snapshot job.

Valid values:

  • STOPPED: The job is not currently running.

  • RUNNING: The job is actively executing.

ResourceSnapshotJobSummary.documentation: An object that contains a Resource Snapshot Job's subset of fields.

ResourceSnapshotJobSummaryList.documentation: A list of summaries of resource snapshot jobs.

OpportunitySummary.documentation: An object that contains an opportunity's subset of fields.

AwsOpportunitySummaryFullView.documentation: Provides a comprehensive view of AwsOpportunitySummaryFullView template.

ResourceSnapshotPayload.documentation: Represents the payload of a resource snapshot. This structure is designed to accommodate different types of resource snapshots, currently supporting opportunity summaries.

ResourceSnapshotRevision.documentation: The revision number of a resource snapshot. The first revision is 1.

Arn.documentation: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the snapshot. This globally unique identifier can be used for cross-service references and in IAM policies.

Revision.documentation: The revision number of the snapshot. This integer value is incremented each time the snapshot is updated, allowing for version tracking of the resource snapshot.

ResourceId.documentation: The identifier of the specific resource snapshotted. The format might vary depending on the ResourceType.

ResourceSnapshotTemplateName.documentation: The name of the template used to create the snapshot.

CreatedBy.documentation: The AWS account ID of the entity that owns the resource from which the snapshot was created.

ResourceSnapshotSummary.documentation: Provides a concise summary of a resource snapshot, including its unique identifier and version information. This structure is used to quickly reference and identify specific versions of resource snapshots.

ResourceSnapshotSummaryList.documentation: A list of summaries of resource snapshots.

ResourceTemplateName.documentation: The name of a template that defines which data a resource snapshot includes. The name contains 3 to 80 letters or digits.

ResourceType.documentation: The type of a resource. The only valid value is Opportunity.

RevenueModel.documentation: The payment type or procurement method that the customer uses to acquire the solution. You can specify Contract, Pay-as-you-go, or Subscription.

SalesActivities.documentation: A list of sales activities that the partner completed for the opportunity.

SalesActivity.documentation: A sales activity that the partner completed for the opportunity.

SalesInvolvementType.documentation: The type of AWS involvement in an opportunity. Valid values are For Visibility Only and Co-Sell.

SearchAwsAccount.documentation: The AWS account ID of the end customer's company.

Specifies the catalog for the request. Valid values:

  • AWS: Production.

  • Sandbox: Testing environments.

Filter.documentation: Specifies a filter tree that narrows the customer accounts. Each node either combines child filters or compares a single field to a value.

Sort.documentation: Specifies the field and direction used to sort the results.

MaxResults.documentation: Specifies the maximum number of results to return in a single call. Use this value together with NextToken to control pagination.

NextToken.documentation: Specifies the token for the next page of results. Use the NextToken value from a previous response to retrieve the next page.

CustomerAccountSummaries.documentation: The customer accounts that match the request.

NextToken.documentation: The token to retrieve the next page of results. This value is absent when there are no more results.

SearchEngagementScore.documentation: A score that AWS assigns to show how likely an opportunity is to succeed. Valid values are High, Medium, and Low.

Catalog.documentation:
Specifies the catalog to search. The following values are valid:

  • AWS: Production.

  • Sandbox: Testing environments.

Keyword.documentation: An optional free-text query string matched against the engagement title, description, customer company name, and member company names. When provided together with Filter or GroupId, each one narrows the result set.

Filter.documentation: A recursive, structured filter tree. Each node is either a boolean combinator (AndAllFilters, OrAllFilters, or NotFilter) or a leaf predicate (a single comparison such as EqualsTo). When provided together with Keyword or GroupId, each one narrows the result set.

GroupId.documentation: The identifier of an engagement group that ListEngagementGroups returns. When you specify a group, the operation returns only the engagements that match the criteria that define the group. The group must be active and available to you in the specified catalog. Otherwise, the request fails with a ValidationException.

Sort.documentation: Specifies the field and direction used to sort the search results. If you omit this field, results are sorted by creation time, newest first.

MaxResults.documentation: Specifies the maximum number of results to return in a single call. If you omit this value, the operation returns up to 20 results. Use this value to control pagination together with NextToken.

NextToken.documentation: A pagination token returned by a previous call. Pass it in a subsequent call to retrieve the next page of results. Omit it on the first call.

EngagementSearchSummaries.documentation: An array of summaries, one for each engagement that matches the request criteria.

NextToken.documentation: A pagination token used to retrieve the next set of results in subsequent calls. The response includes this token only when additional result pages are available.

SearchFilterValue.documentation: A text value that a search filter compares against.

SearchKeyword.documentation: A word or phrase to look for in an opportunity search.

Catalog.documentation: Specifies the catalog in which you run the search. Use AWS to search production opportunities, or use Sandbox to search opportunities in a testing environment.

MaxResults.documentation: The maximum number of results to return in a single call. Use this value to control pagination together with NextToken. If you omit this parameter, the service applies a default page size and returns the remaining results on subsequent pages.

NextToken.documentation: A pagination token returned by a previous call. Pass it in a subsequent call to retrieve the next page of results. Omit it on the first call.

Keyword.documentation: An optional free-text query string matched against opportunity fields. When provided together with Filter, both narrow the result set.

Filter.documentation: A recursive, structured filter tree. Each node is either a boolean combinator (AndAllFilters, OrAllFilters, or NotFilter) or a leaf predicate (a single comparison such as EqualsTo). When provided together with Keyword, both narrow the result set.

Sort.documentation: Specifies the field and direction used to sort the search results.

SearchOpportunitiesRequest.documentation: Contains the request parameters for the SearchOpportunities operation.

OpportunitySearchSummaries.documentation: An array of curated summary views, one for each opportunity that matches the request criteria.

NextToken.documentation: A pagination token for retrieving the next set of results. Pass this token in a subsequent call to get the next page. The response includes this token only when additional result pages are available.

SearchOpportunitiesResponse.documentation: Contains the response that the SearchOpportunities action returns.

Email.documentation: The sender-provided contact's email address associated with the EngagementInvitation.

FirstName.documentation: The sender-provided contact's last name associated with the EngagementInvitation.

LastName.documentation: The sender-provided contact's first name associated with the EngagementInvitation.

BusinessTitle.documentation: The sender-provided contact's title (job title or role) associated with the EngagementInvitation.

Phone.documentation: The sender-provided contact's phone number associated with the EngagementInvitation.

SenderContact.documentation: An object that contains the details of the sender-provided contact person for the EngagementInvitation.

SenderContactEmail.documentation: The email address of an engagement invitation sender.

SenderContactList.documentation: A list of contacts at the sender of an engagement invitation.

Message.documentation: A message that describes which quota the request exceeded.

ServiceQuotaExceededException.documentation:
This error occurs when the request would cause a service quota to be exceeded. Service quotas represent the maximum allowed use of a specific resource, and this error indicates that the request would surpass that limit.

Suggested action: Review the Quotas for the resource, and either reduce usage or request a quota increase.

DeliveryModel.documentation: Specifies the customer's intended payment type agreement or procurement method to acquire the solution or service outlined in the Opportunity.

EffectiveDate.documentation: Specifies the Opportunity's customer engagement start date for the contract's effectiveness.

ExpirationDate.documentation: Specifies the expiration date for the contract between the customer and Amazon Web Services partner. It signifies the termination date of the agreed-upon engagement period between both parties.

SoftwareRevenue.documentation: Specifies a customer's procurement terms details. Required only for partners in eligible programs.

Catalog.documentation: Specifies the catalog in which the solution is hosted, either AWS or Sandbox. This helps partners differentiate between live solutions and those in testing environments.

Id.documentation: Enables the association of solutions (offerings) to opportunities.

Arn.documentation: The SolutionBase structure provides essential information about a solution.

Status.documentation: Specifies the solution's current status, which indicates its state in the system. Valid values: Active | Inactive | Draft. The status helps partners and Amazon Web Services track the solution's lifecycle and availability. Filter for Active solutions for association to an opportunity.

Category.documentation: Specifies the solution category, which helps to categorize and organize the solutions partners offer. Valid values: Software Product | Consulting Service | Hardware Product | Communications Product | Professional Service | Managed Service | Value-Added Resale Amazon Web Services Service | Distribution Service | Training Service | Merger and Acquisition Advising Service.

CreatedDate.documentation: Indicates the solution creation date. This is useful to track and audit.

AwsMarketplaceSolutionArn.documentation: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the AWS Marketplace solution associated with this partner solution.

SolutionBase.documentation: Specifies minimal information for the solution offered to solve the customer's business problem.

SolutionIdentifier.documentation: The identifier of a partner solution. An identifier starts with S- followed by up to 19 digits.

SortOrder.documentation: Specifies the sorting order, either Ascending or Descending. The default is Descending.

SortBy.documentation: Specifies the attribute to sort by, such as Name, CreatedDate, or Status.

SolutionSort.documentation: Configures the solutions' response sorting that enables partners to order solutions based on specified attributes.

SolutionSortName.documentation: The name of the field that sorts a list of solutions.

SolutionStatus.documentation: The status of a partner solution. Active means the solution is available, Inactive means it is no longer available, and Draft means it isn't published yet.

SortBy.documentation: The name of the field that sorts a list of resource snapshot jobs. The only valid value is CreatedDate.
Specifies the field by which to sort the resource snapshot jobs.

SortOrder.documentation: Determines the order in which the sorted results are presented.

SortObject.documentation: Defines the sorting parameters for listing resource snapshot jobs. This structure allows you to specify the field to sort by and the order of sorting.

SortOrder.documentation: The direction of a sort. Valid values are ASCENDING and DESCENDING.

SortableField.documentation: The fields that you can sort customer accounts by.

Stage.documentation: The stage of an opportunity in its lifecycle.

Specifies the catalog for the request. Valid values:

  • AWS: Production.

  • Sandbox: Testing environments.

FileUri.documentation: Specifies the location of the file that contains the customer accounts to create.

StartCustomerAccountBulkJobRequest.documentation: Information about start customer account bulk job request.

Arn.documentation: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the bulk job.

Id.documentation: The unique identifier of the bulk job.

Status.documentation: The current status of the bulk job.

CreatedAt.documentation: The date and time when the bulk job was created.

StartCustomerAccountBulkJobResponse.documentation: Information about start customer account bulk job response.

ClientToken.documentation: A unique, case-sensitive identifier provided by the client that helps to ensure the idempotency of the request. This can be a random or meaningful string but must be unique for each request.

Identifier.documentation: Specifies the unique identifier of the EngagementInvitation to be accepted. Providing the correct identifier helps ensure that the correct engagement is processed.

Tags.documentation: A map of the key-value pairs of the tag or tags to assign.

StartEngagementByAcceptingInvitationTask.documentation: Contains the request parameters for the StartEngagementByAcceptingInvitationTask operation.

TaskId.documentation: The unique identifier of the task, used to track the task’s progress.

TaskArn.documentation: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the task, used for tracking and managing the task within AWS.

StartTime.documentation: The timestamp indicating when the task was initiated. The format follows RFC 3339 section 5.6.

TaskStatus.documentation: Indicates the current status of the task.

Message.documentation: If the task fails, this field contains a detailed message describing the failure and possible recovery steps.

ReasonCode.documentation: Indicates the reason for task failure using an enumerated code.

OpportunityId.documentation: Returns the original opportunity identifier passed in the request. This is the unique identifier for the opportunity.

ResourceSnapshotJobId.documentation: The identifier of the Resource Snapshot Job created as part of this task.

EngagementInvitationId.documentation: Returns the identifier of the engagement invitation that was accepted and used to create the opportunity.

StartEngagementByAcceptingInvitationTask.documentation: Contains the response that the StartEngagementByAcceptingInvitationTask action returns.

Identifier.documentation: The unique identifier of the opportunity from which the engagement task is to be initiated. This helps ensure that the task is applied to the correct opportunity.

AwsSubmission.documentation: Specifies the level of AWS involvement for the opportunity. The value includes the involvement type and the visibility of that involvement.

Tags.documentation: A map of the key-value pairs of the tag or tags to assign.

TaskArn.documentation: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the task, used for tracking and managing the task within AWS.

StartTime.documentation: The timestamp indicating when the task was initiated. The format follows RFC 3339 section 5.6.

TaskStatus.documentation: Indicates the current status of the task. Valid values include IN_PROGRESS, COMPLETE, and FAILED.

Message.documentation: If the task fails, this field contains a detailed message describing the failure and possible recovery steps.

ReasonCode.documentation: Indicates the reason for task failure using an enumerated code.

OpportunityId.documentation: Returns the original opportunity identifier passed in the request, which is the unique identifier for the opportunity created in the partner’s system.

ResourceSnapshotJobId.documentation: The identifier of the resource snapshot job created to add the opportunity resource snapshot to the Engagement. Only populated if TaskStatus is COMPLETE

EngagementId.documentation: The identifier of the newly created Engagement. Only populated if TaskStatus is COMPLETE.

EngagementInvitationId.documentation: The identifier of the new Engagement invitation. Only populated if TaskStatus is COMPLETE.

StartEngagementFromOpportunityTaskRespon.documentation: Contains the response that the StartEngagementFromOpportunityTask action returns.

Specifies the catalog for the request. Valid values:

  • AWS: Production.

  • Sandbox: Testing environments.

ClientToken.documentation: A unique, case-sensitive identifier that you provide to ensure the operation completes no more than one time. If this token matches a previous request with the same parameters, the operation returns the JobId of the original job. If you reuse the token with different parameters, the request fails with a ConflictException.

FileURI.documentation:
Specifies the location of the CSV file that contains the opportunities to create or update. Use one of the following:

  • An s3:// URI of a file that you uploaded to Partner Central for your account. You can add only the versionId query parameter.

  • An https:// presigned Amazon S3 URL

The file must be a plain-text CSV file no larger than 100 MB.

FileFormat.documentation: Specifies the format of the input file. The only supported value is CSV.

StartOpportunityBulkJobRequest.documentation: Specifies the input file location, file format, and client token for starting an opportunity bulk job.

JobId.documentation: The unique identifier of the bulk job. Use it with the other opportunity bulk job operations.

StartOpportunityBulkJobResponse.documentation: The response to a request to start an opportunity bulk job.

Catalog.documentation: Specifies the catalog in which the opportunity creation task is executed. Acceptable values include AWS for production and Sandbox for testing environments.

ClientToken.documentation: A unique token provided by the client to help ensure the idempotency of the request. It helps prevent the same task from being performed multiple times.

Identifier.documentation: The unique identifier of the engagement from which the opportunity creation task is to be initiated. This helps ensure that the task is applied to the correct engagement.

ContextIdentifier.documentation: The unique identifier of the engagement context from which to create the opportunity. This specifies the specific contextual information within the engagement that will be used for opportunity creation.

TaskArn.documentation: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the task, used for tracking and managing the task within AWS.

StartTime.documentation: The timestamp indicating when the task was initiated. The format follows RFC 3339 section 5.6.

TaskStatus.documentation: Indicates the current status of the task.

Message.documentation: If the task fails, this field contains a detailed message describing the failure and possible recovery steps.

ReasonCode.documentation: Indicates the reason for task failure using an enumerated code.

OpportunityId.documentation: The unique identifier of the opportunity created as a result of the task. This field is populated when the task is completed successfully.

ResourceSnapshotJobId.documentation: The identifier of the resource snapshot job created as part of the opportunity creation process.

EngagementId.documentation: The unique identifier of the engagement from which the opportunity was created.

ContextId.documentation: The unique identifier of the engagement context used to create the opportunity.

StartOpportunityFromEngagementTaskRespon.documentation: Contains the response that the StartOpportunityFromEngagementTask action returns.

Catalog.documentation: Specifies the catalog in which the task is initiated. Specify AWS for production environments and Sandbox for testing and development purposes.

Identifiers.documentation: The list of engagement identifiers to include in this prospecting task. Each identifier must correspond to an existing engagement in the specified catalog. Maximum of 100 identifiers per task.

TaskName.documentation: A descriptive name for the task. This name helps identify the task in list and get operations. The name must contain 1 to 128 characters.

ClientToken.documentation: A unique, case-sensitive identifier provided by the client to ensure idempotency. Making the same request with the same ClientToken returns the same response without creating a duplicate task.

StartProspectingFromEngagementTaskReques.documentation: Represents the request structure for starting a prospecting task. Includes up to 100 engagement identifiers and a task name. Uses ClientToken to ensure idempotency.

Identifiers.documentation: The list of engagement identifiers that were accepted into the task queue for processing. This list matches the identifiers provided in the request.

Message.documentation: A message providing additional context about the task's current state. When the task fails, this field contains a detailed description of the failure and suggested recovery steps. This field is only populated for tasks in a failed state.

ReasonCode.documentation: An enumerated code identifying the reason for task failure. This field is only populated when the task has failed. Use the corresponding Message field for a human-readable description of the failure.

StartTime.documentation: The timestamp indicating when the task was initiated. The format follows ISO 8601 date-time notation.

TaskId.documentation: The unique identifier assigned to this task. Use this identifier with GetProspectingFromEngagementTask to retrieve task details and check status.

TaskArn.documentation: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the task. The ARN uniquely identifies the task across AWS and can be used for resource-level IAM policies.

TaskStatus.documentation: The current status of the task. Possible values: PENDING (waiting to run), IN_PROGRESS (actively processing), COMPLETED (successfully processed), and FAILED (unrecoverable error).

StartProspectingFromEngagementTaskRespon.documentation: Represents the response structure returned when a prospecting task is successfully submitted. Contains the task identifier, ARN, and initial status. Uses TaskId with GetProspectingFromEngagementTask to poll for completion.

Catalog.documentation:
Specifies the catalog related to the request. Valid values are:

  • AWS: Starts the request from the production AWS environment.

  • Sandbox: Starts the request from a sandbox environment used for testing or development purposes.

StartResourceSnapshotJobRequest.documentation: Contains the request parameters for the StartResourceSnapshotJob operation.

Specifies the catalog related to the request. Valid values are:

  • AWS: Stops the request from the production AWS environment.

  • Sandbox: Stops the request from a sandbox environment used for testing or development purposes.

ResourceSnapshotJobIdentifier.documentation: The identifier of the job to stop.

StopResourceSnapshotJobRequest.documentation: Contains the request parameters for the StopResourceSnapshotJob operation.

Catalog.documentation:
Specifies the catalog related to the request. Valid values are:

  • AWS: Submits the opportunity request from the production AWS environment.

  • Sandbox: Submits the opportunity request from a sandbox environment used for testing or development purposes.

Identifier.documentation: The identifier of the Opportunity previously created by partner and needs to be submitted.

InvolvementType.documentation:
Specifies the level of AWS sellers' involvement on the opportunity. Valid values:

  • Co-sell: Indicates the user wants to co-sell with AWS. Share the opportunity with AWS to receive deal assistance and support.

  • For Visibility Only: Indicates that the user does not need support from AWS Sales Rep. Share this opportunity with AWS for visibility only, you will not receive deal assistance and support.

Visibility.documentation:
Determines whether to restrict visibility of the opportunity from AWS sales. Default value is Full. Valid values:

  • Full: The opportunity is fully visible to AWS sales.

  • Limited: The opportunity has restricted visibility to AWS sales.

SubmitOpportunityRequest.documentation: Contains the request parameters for the SubmitOpportunity operation.

Tag.documentation: The key-value pair assigned to a specified resource.

ResourceArn.documentation: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the resource that you want to tag.

Tags.documentation: A map of the key-value pairs of the tag or tags to assign.

TagResourceRequest.documentation: Contains the request parameters for the TagResource operation.

TagResourceResponse.documentation: Contains the response of the TagResource operation. The response has no members.

TaggableResourceArn.documentation: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of a resource that you can tag.

AfterTargetCloseDate.documentation: Filters opportunities with a target close date after this date. Use the YYYY-MM-DD format.

BeforeTargetCloseDate.documentation: Filters opportunities with a target close date before this date. Use the YYYY-MM-DD format.

TargetCloseDateFilter.documentation: Filters opportunities based on their target close date.

TaskArn.documentation: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that identifies a task.

TaskArnOrIdentifier.documentation: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) or the identifier of a task. An identifier starts with task- followed by 13 lowercase letters or digits.

TaskIdentifier.documentation: The identifier of a task. An identifier starts with task- followed by 13 lowercase letters or digits.

TaskIdentifiers.documentation: A list of task identifiers or Amazon Resource Names (ARNs).

TaskStatus.documentation: The status of a task. IN_PROGRESS means the task is still running, COMPLETE means it finished successfully, and FAILED means it encountered an error.

Message.documentation: A message that describes why the service throttled the request.

ThrottlingException.documentation:
This error occurs when there are too many requests sent. Review the provided quotas and adapt your usage to avoid throttling.
